The Dyson sphere editor places nodes, frames, and shells on multiple orbital layers around a star, and its power output depends on built structure and absorbed sails.
Dark Fog planetary bases and space hives attack factories and the player's mech, countered by turrets, energy shields, and player combat units.
Dark Fog threat accumulates from the player's power generation and from combat, bases and hives gain levels from experience, and aggressiveness settings scale attack sizes.
Each seed generates a star cluster with star types, planet types, and mineral distributions, including neutron stars, white dwarfs, and black holes.
Layouts are saved and pasted as blueprints, and the mech's construction drones place them.
Planets rotate around their axes and orbit their stars, so solar panel output varies with the local day.
Storage boxes, tanks, and per-slot capacity in logistics stations buffer flows between planets.
The Icarus mech hand-crafts early buildings from inventory before assemblers take over.
The player flies the Icarus mech across planets and through space to build within its range.

The Dyson sphere is designed in a node-and-frame editor and built from solar sails fired by EM-Rail Ejectors and frames carried by rockets; unabsorbed sails expire after 5,400 seconds, and the finished sphere's energy feeds endgame production.
Proliferator coating on input items lets the consuming machine choose extra products or faster production.

Logistics stations set each item slot to local or remote supply, demand, or storage and are paired automatically by priority; up to 100 drones per station haul within a planet and 10 vessels between planets, with range and minimum-load sliders.

name: Dyson Sphere Program
summary: A 3D factory automation game in which the player's mech builds production lines on rotating planets, links star systems with logistics drones and warp vessels, and launches sails and rockets to assemble Dyson spheres around stars.

core_loop: gather from the shared ecosystem -> specialize in skills and craft at tables -> trade through player stores and currencies -> propose and vote on laws and taxes -> research technology to stop the meteor -> manage pollution and species populations before impact
design_notes: Eco makes the ecosystem a shared commons: each player's harvesting and pollution changes species populations and the climate for everyone on the server. Its answer to overexploitation is player-made institutions rather than designer rules, with enforceable laws, taxes, and currencies, and simulation data that players can cite as evidence in debates. It began as an educational project funded in part by the U.S. Department of Education.

mechanics.note: Thousands of plants and animals from dozens of species grow across the world; overhunting or overharvesting can drive a species extinct, and a disruption in one species cascades across the planet.
Mining waste and industrial pollution poison rivers and kill farms, and excessive air pollution raises sea levels.

Players propose laws in a programmable rule system and vote on them, the game enforces ratified laws, and elections set tax rates and community funds; governments range from dictatorships to lawless, trust-based communities.
A meteor is set to strike in thirty days, and players must gather resources and research technology to stop it without harming the world.
Plant and animal populations recover over time unless harvested faster than they regrow; cutting too many trees reduces how much air pollution is absorbed.
Accumulated pollution changes the climate and sea level.
Players run stores and currency exchanges with fiat or resource-backed currencies and set exchange rates.
Players post labor contracts for others to fulfill.
Varied food and larger homes earn skill points spent on specialties such as farming, hunting, trade, and engineering.
More than 30 craft tables turn materials into goods across hundreds of recipes.
Each world is bounded by a meteor due in thirty days, so a server's run ends with stopping it or with impact, and servers are commonly wiped and restarted as fresh worlds.

name: Eco
summary: A multiplayer civilization survival game in which players on one server share a simulated ecosystem, specialize in skills, craft and trade with player-made currencies, and pass enforceable laws while researching how to stop a meteor due in thirty days without wrecking the environment.

core_loop: buy cargo at a station -> hyperspace to a system within fuel range -> fight or evade pirates and police -> dock by matching the station's rotation -> sell for profit -> buy weapons and equipment -> raise combat rating
design_notes: Each of the eight galaxies and its 256 systems is regenerated from a seed rather than stored, which let a large universe fit in an 8-bit micro and made procedural generation the core of the design. Commodity prices differ by system, and fuel limits each hyperjump to 7 light years, so route choice is the main economic decision. The goal of reaching the Elite combat rank is open-ended; the player chooses between trading, piracy, bounty hunting, and mining.

mechanics.note: Eight galaxies of 256 planets each are generated from seed numbers at runtime; each system's name, economy, government, and description derive from the seed.
Commodity prices vary by system economy; the player buys cheap and sells dear between systems, constrained by cargo bay size and the 7 light-year fuel limit per jump.
Real-time wireframe dogfights and manual docking that requires matching a rotating station's spin unless a docking computer is bought.
Legal status (clean, offender, fugitive) worsens with piracy and illegal cargo and draws police ships.
Combat rating rises with kills from Harmless toward Elite; most versions also offer Galactic Navy missions with special rewards.
Mining lasers break asteroids into fragments that can be scooped and sold.

name: Elite
summary: A 3D space trading and combat game in which the player flies a single ship through eight seed-generated galaxies, buying and selling cargo and fighting pirates and police to raise a combat rating.

core_loop: take missions or cargo at a station -> jump between star systems -> trade, fight, mine, or explore -> earn credits, rank, and faction influence -> outfit or buy ships -> background simulation shifts faction control and system states
design_notes: Stellar Forge generates around 400 billion star systems from rules of star and planet formation and blends in about 150,000 systems from real astronomical data, so the galaxy is mostly unvisited. The server-side Background Simulation tracks minor-faction influence, economy, and states per system and updates them from what all players do, so Solo, Private Group, and Open players share one political map. Ship capability comes from outfitting modules within power and mass limits, and flight is Newtonian with a default flight-assist layer.

mechanics.note: One galaxy state is shared by Open, Private Group, and Solo players; Frontier's Background Simulation changes faction influence, system states, and markets over time from aggregate player activity.
Stellar Forge generates a 1:1 Milky Way of about 400 billion systems, bodies, and landable planetary surfaces, blended with about 150,000 catalog systems.
Six-axis Newtonian flight with optional flight assist; manual docking, supercruise approaches, and combat that balances power distributor pips and heat.
Station markets differ by economy type; traders haul commodities between stations for price differences, limited by cargo capacity and jump range.
Market supply and demand at each station shift prices as players buy and sell.
Minor factions hold influence shares per system and enter wars or elections when two factions' influence is close; Powerplay pledges players to one of 12 powers contesting territory.
Standing with minor factions and superpower navy ranks gate missions and system permits.
Mission boards offer delivery, combat, and data missions with deadlines and payouts that also move faction influence.
Ships take modules in fixed slots (power plant, thrusters, frame shift drive, hardpoints); module mass and class set jump range, speed, and loadout.
A power plant's output must cover module draw; over budget, modules shut down by player-set priority.
Ship heat rises from weapons, fuel scooping near stars, and damage; overheating damages modules, and heat sinks dump it.
Mining lasers, collector limpets, and sub-surface charges extract ore from planetary rings.
Squadrons and player-supported minor factions coordinate background simulation work.
System bodies are unknown until scanned; first discoverers are credited.

The power distributor's pips are split among systems, engines, and weapons capacitors in flight, setting each capacitor's recharge; module priorities decide what shuts down when the power plant is over budget.
Each ship module has its own integrity, and damage to the power plant, thrusters, or drive degrades or disables it until repaired.
About 150,000 star systems from real astronomical catalogs are blended into the procedurally generated galaxy.

name: Elite Dangerous
summary: An online space sim set in a 1:1 procedurally generated Milky Way where players trade, fight, mine, and explore while a server-side background simulation shifts faction control from aggregate player actions.

core_loop: plant grasses to spread biomes -> place plants and animals whose requirements are met -> healthy species live longer, breed, and earn diversity points -> spend points on new species, genetic modifications, and evolutions -> complete tasks for rewards
design_notes: Equilinox, built solo by ThinMatrix, ties its economy to ecological fit: each species has a life cycle and requirements, and healthy individuals live longer, breed more, and yield more diversity points, the currency for new species and modifications. Evolution is a gated unlock (meet a species' evolution conditions, then pay to evolve) rather than simulated selection, which keeps the 120+ species on an authored progression. Biomes spread from planted grasses, so terrain type is itself a player-placed stock. Paid genetic modification matches the genome-modification proposal from run catalog-ge.

mechanics.note: Each species needs a biome, food, and nearby plants or water; satisfied individuals stay healthy, live longer, and breed, while unmet needs reduce health.
Species evolve into new species once their conditions are met and points are paid, and 60+ tasks grant points or content.
Diversity points earned by healthy plants and animals are the single currency for buying species, modifications, and evolutions; repeatable tasks let players farm a steady income.
Plants and animals grow, eat, reproduce, and die on species-specific cycles.
Some animals hunt others, so predator placement constrains prey populations.
Planted grasses convert ground into one of 10 biome types, and algae turns water into river for fish.

name: Equilinox
summary: A relaxed nature-building game in which the player spreads biomes with grasses, places plants and animals that each have environmental requirements, and spends diversity points earned by healthy species on evolutions and genetic modifications.

core_loop: take a cargo job -> couple the trailer -> drive the route paying fuel and tolls -> deliver on time with little damage -> earn money and experience -> spend skill points and buy trucks, garages, and drivers -> longer and riskier jobs
design_notes: The pleasure is long-haul driving through a compressed map (71 cities in 12 countries in the base game), with economic pressure from delivery deadlines, fuel, tolls, and repair costs and with damage deducted from pay. Progression is a skill-point tree that unlocks cargo classes (ADR hazardous, long distance, valuable, fragile, urgent, eco driving), plus a company layer in which owned garages host hired AI drivers who earn money off-screen. Multiplayer began as the fan mod TruckersMP in 2013 before official support in 2021.

mechanics.note: Licensed trucks with modeled engines and gearboxes pull trailers whose cargo changes acceleration and braking; collisions damage truck, trailer, and cargo.
Jobs specify cargo, destination, and a time limit; less damage earns more money and experience, while fuel, tolls, and repairs are paid from earnings.
A continuous road map linking European cities sets route distance, tolls, and travel time.
Skill points from experience unlock ADR, long-distance, valuable, fragile, urgent, and eco-driving jobs.
Recruitment agencies supply AI drivers who work from owned garages and return income.
A bank loan is the alternative to saving 100,000 euros for the first truck.
Damage requires paid maintenance at service shops.

name: Euro Truck Simulator 2
summary: A truck driving sim in which the player hauls timed cargo deliveries across a scaled European road network and grows a transport company of trucks, garages, and hired drivers.

core_loop: accrue administrative, diplomatic, and military monarch points -> buy technology, stability, ideas, and development -> steer trade and colonize -> ally and declare wars -> occupy and annex provinces -> manage unrest, estates, and coalitions
design_notes: EU4 converts ruler quality into three spendable currencies (administrative, diplomatic, and military monarch points) that buy technology, stability, ideas, and province development, which makes each succession an economic event. Expansion is checked by systems rather than scripts: aggressive expansion feeds defensive coalitions, and conquered provinces stay restless until integrated. Monarch points, war score, province integration, and missionary conversion are not yet mechanics in the taxonomy (proposals political-capital, war-score-peace, territorial-claims-integration, culture-religion-conversion).

mechanics.note: Alliances, vassals, tributaries, and royal marriages bind nations; aggressive expansion raises other nations' hostility until they form a defensive coalition against the expander.

Trade value generated in provinces flows downstream through a fixed directed network of trade nodes; merchants either collect in a node or steer value toward the player's home node, and trade power in each node sets the share taken.
Provinces accumulate unrest from foreign culture, religion, and recent conquest, and high unrest spawns rebel armies; national stability is a separate stock raised with administrative monarch points.
Administrative, diplomatic, and military technology tracks are bought with matching monarch points; institutions such as feudalism spread between provinces and raise technology cost until embraced.
Estates hold loyalty and influence over the crown and grant bonuses or demands.
Each monarch's administrative, diplomatic, and military skill sets monthly monarch point income; on death an heir succeeds, with risks of regency, succession wars, or personal unions.
AI opinion of the player is an itemized sum of modifiers such as improved relations, royal marriage, and aggressive expansion.
Historical and flavor events fire from national history and current state.
Prestige and power projection modify diplomacy and stability.
Idea groups, policies, and government reforms change national rules.
Deficits are covered by loans, and unmanageable debt ends in bankruptcy.

Administrative, diplomatic, and military monarch points accrue monthly from the ruler's skills (plus advisors) and buy technology, ideas, stability, and province development, so each succession changes the nation's budget of action.

A national corruption value accumulates from several state conditions and falls with a monthly budget line for rooting out corruption; while high it raises the cost of technology and other state actions.
Provinces have a culture and a religion; missionaries convert province religion over time against resistance, and non-state religion or non-accepted culture adds unrest.

Provinces have an owner and a controller; sieges flip control, peace deals transfer ownership, and new provinces must be cored with administrative power, with uncored land adding overextension and unrest.
War score from battles, occupation, and the war goal caps peace demands, each priced in score (provinces, gold, vassalage).
Land battles roll dice each phase of fire and shock, modified by general skill and terrain, and drain each army's strength and morale until one side retreats.

name: Europa Universalis IV
summary: A real-time-with-pause grand strategy game in which the player directs one of over 500 nations from 1444 to 1821 through monarch-point spending, trade-node competition, colonization, diplomacy, and war on a province map.

core_loop: train skills in real time -> mine, salvage, or run missions for materials and ISK -> manufacture or buy ships and modules on the player market -> fit ships and fly into space of a chosen security level -> lose ships in combat and replace them -> corporations and alliances fight over sovereignty
design_notes: EVE keeps one economy for all players: nearly everything is player-made and ship losses are permanent, so wars create manufacturing demand. Risk and reward are tied to space security, with the most profitable activities in low-sec and null-sec, where the NPC police do not destroy aggressors. CCP hired an economist in 2007 to oversee the economy. Security-graded zones and permanent asset loss on destruction are not yet mechanics in the taxonomy (proposals pvp-security-zones, loss-on-death).

mechanics.note: Players gather raw materials and manufacture nearly all ships and modules, then trade them in a supply-and-demand market with price history charts, where manipulation such as ramping and bear raids is possible.

One shared universe on the Tranquility server holds more than 5,000 stargate-linked systems plus about 2,500 wormhole systems; system security from 1.0 to -1.0 sets whether CONCORD police destroy aggressors.
Corporations led by a CEO assign roles, tax members, declare wars for a weekly fee, and join alliances that claim sovereignty over null-sec systems.
Skills have prerequisites, and capital-ship skills take several times longer to train than frigate skills.
Skills train in real time, including while logged off, from a queue of up to 50 skills.
Ships are fitted with modules in high, mid, and low slots plus semi-permanent rigs.
Blueprints turn gathered materials into ships and modules.
Players mine asteroids and salvage wrecks for materials.
Players elect the Council of Stellar Management, which carries requests to CCP; the first election in 2008 had 66 candidates for nine seats.
Unprovoked aggression in secure space costs security status and draws police response.
A destroyed ship and its fittings are gone for good, part of its cargo and modules drops in a lootable wreck, and ship insurance pays back part of the hull's value.

Each system's security from 1.0 to -1.0 decides whether CONCORD police destroy aggressors; high-sec deters player attacks, low- and null-sec leave them to players, and the riskier zones hold the richer activities.

name: EVE Online
summary: A single-universe space MMO in which players mine, manufacture, trade, and fight in ships that are destroyed for good, inside a player-made economy and a galaxy of high-, low-, and null-security space where player alliances claim sovereignty.

core_loop: type to or touch Grace and Trip -> parser maps input to a discourse act -> characters react and tension shifts -> drama manager picks the next beat -> secrets surface -> the couple reconciles, splits, or throws the player out
design_notes: Michael Mateas and Andrew Stern built Façade as a research artifact: Grace and Trip are written in A Behavior Language (ABL) as reactive behaviors, and a drama manager picks the next story beat from an authored library to follow a tension arc toward a climax. Typed text is mapped to a small set of discourse acts (the Versu paper counts 30 parameterized speech acts and 27 beats), which lets a limited body of authored dialogue answer open-ended input. It is a boundary case: the simulated systems are the parser, character behaviors, and beat sequencing over mostly authored dialogue, built for replay so players can find other outcomes.

mechanics.note: Typed sentences are matched by keywords and context to discourse acts such as agreeing, criticizing, or flirting, which Grace and Trip answer in character.
A drama manager chooses the next beat whose preconditions match the state, steering toward a rising tension arc and one of three endings.
Revelations such as a confessed affair fire only when earlier beats and player choices set them up.
As the couple argues, the player's responses read as taking one side, which shapes later beats.
The player walks around the apartment in first person and can click objects or body parts to hug, comfort, or kiss.

name: Façade
summary: A free 2005 interactive drama in which the player types natural language as a dinner guest of the married couple Grace and Trip while a drama manager sequences authored beats toward one of three endings.

claims.text: Factorio was publicly purchasable as an alpha from its official site in 2013, after the February 2013 Indiegogo campaign, three years before Steam early access on 2016-02-25; `year` records the 2013 alpha.
The design grew out of the Minecraft tech mods IndustrialCraft and BuildCraft, which lead designer Michal Kovarik cited; the `influenced_by` edge to Minecraft records that mod lineage.

core_loop: mine ore -> smelt and assemble on belts and inserters -> feed science packs to labs -> research new machines -> pollution draws biter attacks -> defend and expand outposts by rail -> launch a rocket
design_notes: Lead designer Michal Kovarik cited the Minecraft tech mods IndustrialCraft and BuildCraft; Factorio turned their pipes and machines into a standalone game where ratio planning and layout are the challenge. Item movement is discrete and deterministic (belts carry 15, 30, 45, or 60 items per second across two lanes), which makes throughput legible and lets the lockstep multiplayer simulate identical worlds. Pollution couples industry to combat: chunks above 15 units diffuse 2% to neighbors, spawners that absorb it send attack groups, and total pollution produced drives the enemy evolution factor. Each layer of logistics (belts, trains with block signals, roboport-based logistic and construction robots, circuit combinators) is a mechanic the player adopts when the previous one stops scaling, and blueprints let solved layouts be reused. Speed, productivity, and efficiency modules and beacons that trade power for throughput, and the rocket silo as a terminal sink for produced parts, have no taxonomy entry; this run proposed both.

mechanics.note: Assembling machines, furnaces, chemical plants, and refineries run fixed recipes with crafting times; science packs require multi-step trees from ore to circuits, oil products, and rocket parts.
Two-lane belts in four tiers carry 15, 30, 45, or 60 items per second; splitters, undergrounds, and lane priorities shape flow, and inserters move items between belts and machines.
Labs consume science packs of rising recipe complexity to research a technology graph that leads through oil processing, robots, and nuclear power to the rocket silo.
Electric and burner mining drills extract iron, copper, coal, stone, and uranium from ore patches at rates set by drill tier and mining productivity research; pumpjacks extract crude oil.
Machines emit pollution into 32x32 chunks; above 15 units a chunk diffuses 2% to each cardinal neighbor every 64 ticks, and water, grass, and trees absorb it.

Biter and spitter nests send attack groups when their chunk absorbs pollution, recruiting units at pollution costs from 4 for a small biter to 400 for a behemoth; turrets, walls, and flamethrowers defend.
An evolution factor rises with elapsed time, total pollution produced, and spawners destroyed, squashed as total over one plus total, and unlocks medium, big, and behemoth enemies.
Steam engines, solar panels, accumulators, and nuclear reactors feed a pole-connected grid; under shortage power is shared evenly so all machines slow proportionally.
Selected areas save to blueprints, books, and a personal library that persists across saves; exchange strings are shared online, and construction robots build pasted ghosts.
Rail and chain signals divide track into blocks that one train reserves at a time, letting train networks share track.
Trains run schedules of stations with wait conditions on cargo, time, inactivity, or circuit signals.
Red and green wires carry item-count signals into arithmetic, decider, constant, and (in 2.0) selector combinators that control inserters, belts, train stops, and lamps.
Pipes and pumps carry water, crude oil, petroleum, and steam; version 2.0 merged pipes into segments that share contents.
Ore tiles run out as they are mined, and crude oil wells decline toward a 20% yield floor, pushing expansion to new patches.
Chests, storage tanks, and the logistic network's storage chests buffer items, and full outputs stall machines upstream.
The engineer crafts early buildings and items from inventory using the same recipes as assemblers, with a crafting queue.
The Space Age expansion adds five quality levels from normal to legendary, raised by chance from quality modules, with a recycler that returns 25% of ingredients.
In Space Age, Gleba's agricultural products spoil over fixed timers into spoilage, and recipe outputs inherit ingredient freshness.
Mods use a modified Lua 5.2 with data and control stages and are distributed through an in-game mod portal; overhauls such as Krastorio 2 replace progression.
Production and consumption graphs per item over time windows and an electric network panel show where ratios fail.
Maps are generated from a seed with settings for ore frequency, size, and richness, water, cliffs, and enemy bases.
Space Age elevated rails let a second track layer cross over ground tracks and buildings.
The engineer walks the map, mines by hand early, and places buildings within reach, later driving cars, tanks, and spidertrons.
The rocket silo consumes rocket parts for each launch, and launching a rocket ends the base game; Space Age moves the goal to a space platform reaching the edge of the solar system.

Speed, productivity, efficiency, and (Space Age) quality modules fill machine slots, and beacons project module effects onto neighboring machines at a power cost; productivity bonuses are capped at +300%.

Roboports define logistic zones where logistic robots carry items among active provider, passive provider, storage, buffer, and requester chests by priority, one item per trip at 3 tiles per second before research.
Straight and curved rail pieces are placed to build train networks, with elevated rails in Space Age, and the rail planner lays segments between points.

name: Factorio
summary: A factory automation game in which the player builds belt, train, robot, and circuit networks that mine, refine, and assemble items on an alien planet while pollution provokes native biters that evolve over time.

core_loop: buy fields and machinery -> plow, seed, fertilize, and harvest with implements -> store or sell crops or feed productions and animals -> take contracts for extra income -> reinvest in land, buildings, and equipment
design_notes: Farming Simulator models agriculture as ordered field operations performed with specific implements, so the challenge is machine operation and fleet logistics rather than market strategy. FS25 lists 25 crop types including two rice varieties grown in paddies, spinach, peas, and green beans, adds water buffalo and goats, adds twisters and hail that damage crops, and deforms soft ground under tires. Dynamically generated contracts pay for work on other farms, and the in-game ModHub distributes developer-tested community vehicles, maps, and scripts.

mechanics.note: Fields move through cultivating or plowing, seeding, fertilizing, weeding, and harvesting with matching implements; 25 crop types follow seasonal calendars, with rice grown in paddies.
The player drives over 400 licensed vehicles and implements from more than 150 brands, each with its own power, speed, and weight; GPS-assisted steering automates straight passes.
Vehicles accumulate wear and damage that reduce performance until repaired at a workshop.
Tires leave tracks that deform soft ground.
Cows, sheep, pigs, chickens, horses, water buffalo, and goats with offspring need feed and care and yield products.
Productions and farm shops convert crops into processed goods as business ventures.
Dynamically generated contracts such as mowing, fertilizing, or hauling pay for work on other farmers' fields.
Hired AI helpers drive vehicles to work fields while the player does other tasks.
A seasonal cycle, introduced in FS22, sets planting and harvest windows.
Twisters and hail can damage crops.
Bank loans fund early expansion.
ModHub distributes developer-tested community mods that add vehicles, maps, and scripts.

name: Farming Simulator 25
summary: The 2024 entry in Giants Software's series in which the player runs a farm business by operating over 400 licensed vehicles and implements across seasonal field work, livestock, forestry, and production chains.

core_loop: gather, hunt, forage, and farm -> rotate crops to hold soil fertility -> feed a varied diet and supply clean water, clothing, and healers against disease -> upgrade housing and the town center as desirability rises -> fortify against raiders drawn by prosperity
design_notes: Farthest Frontier makes public health the main failure path: dysentery, cholera, tetanus, rabies, frostbite, and bubonic plague each have causes the player can address with clean water, clothing and shoes, healers, and rat catchers. Farming adds soil state, with 12 crops that must be rotated and fields improved by clearing weeds and rocks, and 19 food types with berries and greens preventing scurvy. Prosperity raises raider strength, so growth itself increases military pressure.

mechanics.note: Twelve crops with rotation to preserve soil fertility; fields improve by clearing weeds and rocks and adjusting the soil mix.
Dysentery, cholera, tetanus, rabies, frostbite, and plague spread or strike based on water, clothing, rats, and healer coverage.
Nineteen food types; diet variety, including berries and greens against scurvy, is needed for health.
Rising prosperity draws stronger raiders and foreign armies; difficulty is adjustable and pacifist mode removes them.
Palisades, stone walls, towers, barracks, and equipped soldiers.
Housing and the town center advance through tiers as prosperity and desirability grow.
Desirability from surroundings gates housing upgrades.
A tree of over 140 points of upgrades.
Crafted goods are traded for resources the town lacks.

name: Farthest Frontier
summary: A frontier-town city builder in which crop rotation, soil fertility, diet variety, clean water, and healers decide whether named diseases spread, while prosperity draws stronger raiders against walled defenses.

core_loop: scout and sign players -> set tactics and training -> the match engine simulates fixtures from attributes and instructions -> morale, form, and finances shift -> the board and fans judge results -> rebuild the squad over seasons
design_notes: Football Manager simulates the whole football world from a database of real players, staff, and clubs maintained by fan researchers, with tens of thousands of players developing, aging, and moving in loaded leagues. Matches are simulated from player attributes and tactical instructions and shown through a 2D engine in FM 2005 and a 3D engine from FM 2009. Information is uncertain: scouts and analysts reveal attributes and fit, and scout knowledge of an area is tracked (as 0 to 100 percent from FM 2018). Everton agreed in 2008 to use the database for scouting. Contract and transfer talks and the board's job-security judgment have no matching mechanics in the taxonomy (proposed as negotiation and board-confidence). The series began as Championship Manager in 1992 and was relaunched under this name with FM 2005 in 2004.

mechanics.note: Fixtures are simulated event by event from each player's attributes, condition, and morale and the manager's tactics and touchline instructions, shown in 2D or 3D.
Players' attributes are shown only as well as the club's scouts know them; scout knowledge accumulates per region and is shown as a percentage from FM 2018.
Players and staff are signed through transfers, loans, and contracts with wages, bonuses, and agents.
Player attributes develop through training schedules, match experience, and coaching quality up to individual potential.
Players peak and decline with age, retire, and are replaced by yearly youth intakes.
Generated youth players enter the database each season alongside the real ones.
Personality and hidden attributes such as professionalism affect development and reactions.
Squad hierarchy, cohesion, and player opinions of the manager are tracked from FM 2018.
Team talks and private conversations with players praise, criticize, or promise, changing morale.
Press conferences pose questions with answer options that change morale and media relations.
Club and manager reputation set who will sign; board and fan confidence decide whether the manager is sacked.
Club finances cover wage and transfer budgets, with taxes added in FM 2013.
Data analysts and statistics screens report player and team performance.
Transfer fees are negotiated with selling clubs and contracts with players and their agents over wages, length, bonuses, and clauses, and talks can break down.
The board sets season expectations and, with fan confidence, judges results against them; falling confidence brings warnings and then sacking.

name: Football Manager
summary: A football club management series in which the player sets tactics, training, transfers, and finances while a match engine simulates games from the attributes of players drawn from a researched database of real footballers.

core_loop: paint residential, road, patrol, and forestry zones -> villagers build homes inside them -> assign workers and production chains -> trade with neighbors and pay taxes -> advance Labor, Clergy, or Kingdom estates -> assemble monuments from parts
design_notes: Foundation separates intent from layout: the player paints areas for homes, roads, patrols, and forestry, and housing appears inside them without a grid. Major buildings are not fixed footprints but assemblies of parts, so a monument's function and capacity follow from the modules chosen. Progress runs along three estates, which can be specialized or combined.

mechanics.note: A painting tool marks areas for homes, roads, patrol routes, and forest extraction; homes fill residential zones organically.
Buildings and monuments are assembled from individual parts whose choice sets function and appearance.
Buildings are placed and rotated without a grid.
Trade with neighboring villages.
Progress unlocks through tiers guided by a book, along Labor, Clergy, or Kingdom estates.

name: Foundation
summary: A gridless medieval city builder in which painted zones grow homes organically, monuments are assembled from modular parts, and the village advances along Labor, Clergy, or Kingdom estates.

core_loop: carry sand, water, and lava with the Breath -> reshape terrain to open paths -> send villagers to totems to found villages -> vegetation spreads across soil -> divert tsunamis, floods, fires, and eruptions -> unlock powers and reach the portal
design_notes: Designed by Eric Chahi and presented as a spiritual successor to Populous, it replaces discrete land raising with a continuous material simulation: water flows and erodes, lava cools into solid rock, and soil lets vegetation spread once a village is founded, fast enough that islands can be reshaped within minutes. The cursor, called the Breath, carries matter and changes appearance to match it, replacing a conventional HUD. Disasters are announced shortly before they hit, so each map alternates between building and short preparation windows.

mechanics.note: The Breath picks up and deposits sand, water, and lava in real time to build land bridges, dams, and barriers.
Water flows over the terrain, erodes it, and floods low ground and villages; tsunamis sweep across islands.
Lava cools into solid rock, water erodes soil, fire burns vegetation, and powers can jellify or remove water.
Powers such as jellifying water are granted by completing objectives; magical stones protect against water and fire.
Tsunamis and eruptions, announced shortly before by shamans.
Wildfires spread through vegetation and can be extinguished.
Villagers are sent to totems to found villages.
Each map is cleared by settling every totem to open a portal.

name: From Dust
summary: A god game in which the player carries sand, water, and lava across islands whose material simulation erodes, floods, and hardens terrain, protecting a tribe as it founds villages at totems.

core_loop: keep the coal generator fueled -> heat districts and insulate buildings as temperatures fall -> assign workers to gather coal, wood, steel, and food -> sign laws that trade welfare for productivity -> balance hope and discontent -> survive the storm
design_notes: The city is radial around one generator that heats a circular area, so layout is a function of heat range and fuel, and a coal shortage or overload can end the run. The Book of Laws sequences laws so that early compromises such as child labor or extended shifts open harsher later options, and Order or Faith paths lead toward totalitarian rule, turning policy into moral pressure tracked by hope and discontent. Building heat versus falling outside temperature has no exact taxonomy mechanic (see run proposal); 11 bit studios cites This War of Mine as the origin of its aim for meaningful entertainment, now applied to a whole society.

mechanics.note: The Book of Laws offers adaptation laws such as child labor, extended shifts, and prosthetics, plus Order or Faith paths whose later laws are harsher.
Hope and Discontent meters respond to laws, events, and conditions; hope too low or discontent too high for too long ends the game in revolt.
Temperature falls on a schedule toward the Great Storm, which the main scenario must be survived through.
The generator heats a circular area whose range and level the player raises; buildings outside heat need insulation or heaters.
Coal, wood, steel, and food come from thumpers, sawmills, mines, and hunters.
Workers, engineers, and children fill different job types.
Citizens work daylight shifts; emergency shifts extend hours at a cost.
Scouts explore the frozen wasteland map for survivors and resources, the only way to grow the workforce.
Individual decisions, such as how to handle an injured child, offer choices that shift hope and discontent.
Workshops research heat, extraction, and automaton technologies.

name: Frostpunk
summary: A survival city builder in which the leader of the last city around a coal generator must keep falling temperatures at bay while signing laws that trade citizens' welfare against productivity under hope and discontent meters.

core_loop: build food, housing, extraction, and industry districts -> heat districts from the generator -> factions propose ideas and laws -> negotiate council votes -> faction tension rises or falls -> survive whiteouts and found colonies
design_notes: Frostpunk 2 moves from single buildings to districts and from one leader's decree to a council: 100 delegates, each tied to a faction, vote on every proposed law, with 51 votes for most laws and two thirds for laws that expand the Steward's power. Negotiated promises that are not kept anger factions, and tension between factions can escalate into murder and civil war, so the developer describes social survival as more important than environmental threats. Population is handled as district-level aggregates rather than individual workers.

mechanics.note: Districts for food, housing, extraction, and industry are placed on frost; buildings inside add functions.
A council of 100 faction delegates votes on each proposed law; 51 votes pass most laws, two thirds pass laws that grant the Steward more power.
Factions with conflicting ideals react to adopted ideas and laws; radicals grow within factions.
Laws are proposed, negotiated with promises, and enacted when the council approves.
Faction tension can escalate into murder and civil war.
An Idea Tree of faction-proposed ideas to solve problems.
Whiteouts are severe storms prepared for with fuel reserves.
Food, coal, oil, and steam come from frostland deposits and districts.
Utopia Builder mode sets an objective and optional challenges that fail the run if missed.

name: Frostpunk 2
summary: The sequel to Frostpunk, in which the Steward builds whole districts on the frost and must pass laws through a council of 100 faction delegates while faction tension can escalate into civil war.

core_loop: jump to a beacon -> resolve an event or fight -> allocate reactor power and direct crew under fire -> repair breaches, fires, and systems -> spend scrap on upgrades -> stay ahead of the rebel fleet to the flagship
design_notes: FTL models a ship as rooms with oxygen levels, doors, systems, and crew positions; hits create breaches, fires, and system damage that crew must walk to and repair, so a combat is a spatial triage problem as well as a damage race. The reactor's power bars are the central budget shared by shields, engines, weapons, oxygen, and medbay, and the player shifts them during paused combat. Manual reactor power allocation and per-system damage that removes capacity until repaired have no dedicated taxonomy ids (power-grid is the closest fit); both are recorded as new-mechanic proposals.

mechanics.note: Each room has an oxygen level that equalizes through open doors, drains through hull breaches and opened airlocks, and is refilled by the oxygen system; crew suffocate in empty rooms.
Hits and events start fires that spread between rooms, damage systems and crew, and burn oxygen; crew extinguish them or the player vents the room.
Each jump advances the rebel fleet across the sector map; overtaken beacons yield hard fights and no reward, forcing a trade between exploration and speed.
Losing the ship or all crew ends the run and deletes the save; dead crew members are gone.
Crew gain skill in piloting, engines, shields, weapons, repair, and combat through use, improving station bonuses.
Eight species have fixed traits such as faster repair, fire immunity, or extra combat damage.
The player moves crew between rooms to man stations, repair systems and breaches, fight boarders, and put out fires; crew act on their own only within the room they occupy.
Each sector is a generated map of about twenty beacons with stores, hazards, and events.
Beacon events offer text choices, with extra options unlocked by specific crew, systems, or equipment, and some quests chain across beacons.
Beacon contents are unknown until visited unless revealed by upgrades such as long-range scanners.
Pause is the main tactical tool for issuing orders mid-combat.

Reactor power bars are assigned among shields, engines, weapons, oxygen, medbay, and other systems, usually while paused in combat; each system caps how many bars it accepts, and damage removes usable bars until crew repair it.
Each weapon shot rolls against the target's evasion, shield layers absorb hits, and hits damage the room and the system inside it.

Hits damage the system in the struck room (shields, weapons, engines, oxygen, piloting), removing its usable power bars until crew repair it, and the player targets enemy rooms to disable specific systems.

name: FTL: Faster Than Light
summary: A roguelite starship sim where the player allocates reactor power and directs crew through room-level oxygen, fire, breach, and system-damage simulation while fleeing a rebel fleet across eight sectors.

core_loop: choose topic, genre, platform, and audience -> allocate focus across three development stages -> design and technology points accumulate with bugs -> reviews score the game -> sales and fans -> research, engines, and hires
design_notes: Game Dev Tycoon reduces game making to a configuration problem scored by a hidden market model: each topic and genre pair, each genre and audience pair, and each platform carry fit weights, and each genre favors a particular split of effort across the development stages. Review scores compare the new game against the player's previous best, so the bar rises as the studio improves. A fictional timeline of parody consoles enters and leaves the market from the 1980s onward, which forces platform bets (date-driven availability is proposed as dated-tech-timeline). Greenheart released its own cracked copy in which piracy bankrupts the in-game studio.

mechanics.note: Each game is a topic, genre, platform, and audience pick plus focus sliders across three development stages; reviews score its fit and quality against the studio's best.
After moving out of the garage, the player hires designers and programmers with design, technology, and speed stats and assigns them to development tasks.
Research points unlock new topics, genres, and engine features; custom engines bundle researched features and raise technology output.
Staff gain experience and can be sent to training to raise stats or specialize.
Salaries, office upkeep, and development costs drain cash between releases; running out ends the game.
Bigger offices, R&D and hardware labs, and larger projects unlock as money and fans grow.
A fan count from past releases scales sales of future games.
Industry news, console launches, and studio events fire on a fixed historical timeline.
Mods are written in JavaScript through the gdt-modAPI and shared on the Steam Workshop.
Marketing campaigns bought during development raise a game's hype, which boosts its launch sales.
Fictional consoles launch and retire on a fixed in-game calendar from the 1980s onward, so platform choice is a bet on a console's remaining market life.

name: Game Dev Tycoon
summary: A game-studio business sim where the player picks topic, genre, and platform for each game, splits development effort across design and technology focus areas, and lives or dies by review scores across the history of the industry.

core_loop: place live cells on the grid -> apply birth on 3 and survival on 2 or 3 neighbors to every cell at once -> pattern stabilizes, oscillates, dies, or emits gliders -> observe -> edit the seed and rerun
design_notes: Conway's rule is the minimal case of emergence from local update: each cell's next state depends only on how many of its eight neighbors are alive, all cells update simultaneously, and the only input is the initial pattern. The rule is Turing complete, so whether an arbitrary pattern stops changing is undecidable, and decades of discovery (Gosper's period-30 glider gun of November 1970, the R-pentomino's 1,103-generation run) came from players searching seeds. Simulators such as Golly add Hashlife for large time jumps and scripting for rule variants. The rule itself is not yet a mechanic in the taxonomy (proposal cellular-automaton-rule), so the decomposition records seeding, stepping, and run speed.

mechanics.note: The player's only act is toggling cells on the grid to set the seed before running generations.
Computer implementations step one generation at a time or run continuously; later simulators such as Golly use Hashlife to jump far ahead in time.
Each generation is a discrete synchronous update the player can step through one at a time.

name: Conway's Game of Life
summary: A zero-player cellular automaton on an infinite square grid in which each cell lives or dies by the B3/S23 neighbor-count rule, producing gliders, oscillators, and universal computation from a seeded pattern.

core_loop: spawn props, ragdolls, and NPCs -> move and freeze them with the physics gun -> weld, rope, and motor them with the tool gun -> test the contraption or scene -> share it, or play a community game mode built on the same tools
design_notes: Garry's Mod exposes the Source engine's rigid-body physics directly: the physics gun grabs, rotates, and freezes any prop, and the tool gun adds welds, ropes, axles, motors, thrusters, and other constraints, so contraptions are built from rigid bodies and joints. Its larger contribution is that the whole game is scriptable in Lua and servers download addons on join, so most play happens inside player-made game modes such as Trouble in Terrorist Town, Prop Hunt, and DarkRP, and the add-on Wiremod adds sensors and logic gates. Garry's Mod began as a free Half-Life 2 mod in 2004 and became a paid Steam product in 2006.

mechanics.note: Every spawned prop and ragdoll is a physics object; the physics gun lifts, rotates, and freezes them, and collisions, gravity, and buoyancy follow the Source physics engine.
The tool gun joins props with welds, ropes, axles, sliders, winches, motors, wheels, and thrusters, turning loose props into vehicles and machines.
A Lua API covers entities, weapons, HUD, and game rules; servers send addons to clients on join, and community game modes (TTT, Prop Hunt, DarkRP) became the main way people play.
The player is a first-person character who walks, flies with noclip, and wields the physics and tool guns.
Steam Workshop distributes saves, dupes, maps, and addons.
The Wiremod addon adds wires, sensors, gates, and programmable chips to contraptions.
The duplicator tool and Advanced Duplicator addon copy and paste multi-prop contraptions.

name: Garry's Mod
summary: A Source engine physics sandbox in which players spawn props, ragdolls, and NPCs, join them with welds and constraints, and script whole new multiplayer game modes in Lua.

aliases: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior

claims.text: In the two-day end-to-end run, relationship network density rose from 0.167 to 0.74 and five agents attended the Valentine's Day party.

core_loop: agents perceive nearby events and objects -> observations enter the memory stream -> retrieve memories by recency, importance, and relevance -> plan the day and react -> converse and act -> reflections summarize memories -> plans and relationships change
design_notes: Park and colleagues replace authored behavior trees with a loop of language-model calls on gpt-3.5-turbo. Every observation is stored as text with timestamps; retrieval scores memories by recency (decay 0.995 per game hour), importance (rated 1-10 by the model when stored), and embedding relevance, each normalized and weighted equally. When the summed importance of recent events passes 150 (two or three times a day) the agent writes reflections, and plans are decomposed from a day outline into hour and 5-15 minute chunks. Seeding one agent with the intent to host a Valentine's Day party led to 13 of 25 agents hearing about it and five attending over two game days, at a cost of thousands of dollars in API credits. The open-source release steps the town 10 game seconds per step.

mechanics.note: Each agent's memory stream stores observations, plans, and reflections as text; retrieval ranks them by recency (0.995 decay per game hour), model-rated importance (1-10), and embedding relevance, and reflections fire when summed importance exceeds 150.
Each morning the model drafts a day plan of about five to eight broad chunks, decomposed into hour-long and then 5-15 minute actions that agents revise when they react to events.

Information spreads only through agent conversations; over two game days awareness of a mayoral candidacy rose from 1 to 8 agents and of a party from 1 to 13, with 6 of 453 awareness answers hallucinated.
Plans, dialogue, importance ratings, and reflections are all generated by gpt-3.5-turbo calls at runtime.
Users address agents in natural language as a persona or as the agent's inner voice, and can rewrite the status of objects in natural language.
Researchers interview agents and read their memory streams to evaluate believability.
Agents form acquaintances through conversation; network density rose from 0.167 to 0.74 over two game days.

name: Generative Agents (Smallville)
summary: A research sandbox in which 25 language-model agents in a Sims-like town keep natural-language memory streams, reflect, and plan their days, producing unscripted information spread and social coordination.

core_loop: dig into and build up voxel terrain -> assign settlers to roles and jobs -> settlers meet needs and mood shifts -> seasons change food supply -> raiders and beasts attack the walls -> research, build higher, and take in newcomers
design_notes: It follows the RimWorld pattern of named settlers with traits, perks, skills, needs, and moods, and is widely compared to RimWorld and Dwarf Fortress. Its distinctive layer is a fully three-dimensional voxel map: the player can dig cellars and caverns, raise multi-storey stone and timber forts, and reshape earth and water, so defensive geometry and storage depth are design problems in three dimensions. Early access ran from June 2021 to the 1.0 release in March 2026.

mechanics.note: A 3D terrain toolset digs out or fills voxel earth and water on a randomly generated multi-level map, so cellars, moats, and caverns are carved from the ground.
Settlements stack multi-storey buildings above ground and cellars and caverns below, connected by stairs and ladders.
Settlers track needs such as hunger, sleep, clothing preferences, and religion, and meeting them keeps settlers content.
Repeated bandit raids and animal attacks are met with walls, traps, and settlers equipped and commanded in battle.
Settlers in poor conditions become dissatisfied and may leave the settlement.
Backgrounds, traits, and perks set at settler creation.
Skills such as Animal Handling improve through use, including hunting and combat.
Settlers are assigned to roles that fit their skills.
Built structures need support, and unsupported sections collapse.
Workshops, chapels, libraries, and bedrooms are furnished and decorated rooms.
Seasonal changes govern food production and storage.
Food keeps longer in cool storage such as cellars.
Research unlocks medieval technology.

name: Going Medieval
summary: A colony sim set after a plague in which settlers with traits, needs, and moods dig into and build up a multi-level voxel terrain to survive seasons and raids.

core_loop: pass license tests -> enter championships -> win credits and prize cars -> buy cars and performance parts -> tune the car -> enter higher-class events
design_notes: Simulation mode made car ownership and driving skill the progression: driver's licenses earned through timed tests gate events, and credits from championships buy cars, parts, and tuning. Reviewers singled out the handling model and the tuning freedom, and criticized license tests that could be harder than the races they unlocked. It was the first game designed for the DualShock's analog control and rumble, and IGN called it the grandfather of modern console racing sims.

mechanics.note: Each of 140 cars has its own handling that responds to parts and tuning; reviewers rated it above any earlier racing game.
Simulation mode requires earning driver's licenses through timed tests before entering higher events.
Credits and prize cars build a garage drawn from 140 production cars.
The first game designed for DualShock analog control and rumble; license tests and races grade precise braking and cornering.
Credits buy performance parts and tuning that tailor a car to the player's driving style.
Championships award trophies, credits, and prize cars.

name: Gran Turismo
summary: A PlayStation racing game that paired a tuned handling model and 140 production cars with license tests, prize credits, and parts tuning in a Simulation mode career.

claims.text: GT Sophy 2.0 was added to Gran Turismo 7 as a rival in Quick Race across nine tracks and 340 cars in November 2023.
In 2025 GT Sophy 2.1 extended to Custom Race with tuning, tire, and fuel options.

core_loop: buy or tune a car -> race against AI or players -> earn credits -> expand the collection -> harder events
design_notes: Included because it is the clearest shipped case of a learned opponent in a simulation game. GT Sophy, trained with model-free deep reinforcement learning on parallel simulator instances, became selectable as a permanent rival in 2023 and was extended to custom races in 2025, one content update at a time.

mechanics.note: Tire, suspension, aerodynamics, and drivetrain models per car; tuning parts and settings change handling.
Racing lines, braking points, and throttle control on wheel or pad decide results; GT Sophy is trained to the same physics.

name: Gran Turismo 7
summary: A console racing simulator that combines a detailed vehicle dynamics model and car collection with GT Sophy, a deep reinforcement learning opponent added as a permanent rival in 2023.

claims.text: Hamurabi derives from The Sumerian Game (1964) by Mabel Addis and William McKay; Dyment wrote the FOCAL version after learning of it, and David Ahl expanded it in BASIC.

core_loop: read the steward's yearly report -> trade grain for land at a random price -> allocate grain to food and seed -> harvest, rats, arrivals, and plague resolve -> next year
design_notes: Three stocks (people, acres, bushels of grain) and three yearly allocations make the whole game one stock-and-flow puzzle: grain is food, seed, and the currency for land at once, so every bushel has competing uses. Randomness enters only through harvest yield, rat losses, a land price of 17 to 26 bushels per acre, arrivals, and a plague that halves the population, so the player manages expected value under variance. Dyment wrote it in FOCAL for the PDP-8 from a description of The Sumerian Game (1964); David Ahl's BASIC version spread it as a type-in listing and seeded Kingdom, Dukedom, and Santa Paravia en Fiumaccio.

mechanics.note: Ten rounds, each one year: a status report, then three typed decisions (acres to buy or sell, bushels to feed, acres to plant) before the year resolves.
People must be fed grain each year; if at least 45 percent starve in one round the game ends early.
Planted acres consume seed grain and return a random yield per acre at year end; each person can farm only a set amount of land, so labor caps planting.
Each year carries a chance of plague that halves the population.
Rats eat a random amount of stored grain each year, a loss on holding stock.
Each round opens with a steward's report of births, deaths, harvest, rat losses, and land price.

name: Hamurabi
summary: A ten-turn text game in which the player, as the Babylonian king Hammurabi, splits a grain stock between feeding people, planting acres, and buying land while harvests, rats, and plague vary at random.

core_loop: start a shift -> scan the ship -> vent pressure and make power, fuel, coolant, and reactor systems safe -> cut parts free -> grapple them to the correct receptacle -> salvage value pays down debt -> buy tool upgrades
design_notes: Each ship is a physics assembly of joined parts and typed hazards rather than an authored level: cutting into a pressurized room causes explosive decompression, cutting live electrical wires or coolant pipes can explode, and a reactor removed from its casing must be delivered before it melts down. The order of disassembly is the puzzle, and the taxonomy lacks a mechanic for it (proposed as salvage-deconstruction). Oxygen and thruster fuel act as survival stocks, and shifts are timed except in Open Shift mode.

mechanics.note: Ships are assemblies of separable parts; freed parts keep mass and momentum in zero gravity and are pulled or flung with the tether grapple toward the right receptacle.
The laser cutter severs structure at cut points and joints; cutting live electrical wires or coolant pipes can cause an explosion, so where and in what order to cut is the core decision.

Systems must be made safe in order: pressurized rooms vented, electrical and coolant lines avoided, and reactors delivered before they melt down; mistakes produce the physical result rather than an error.
Rooms hold atmosphere, and an uncontrolled decompression flushes the player and loose objects out of the ship.
Oxygen and thruster fuel deplete during a shift and must be replenished.
Shifts are timed; Open Shift mode removes the limit.
The character owes $1.2 billion to Lynx Corporation, and salvage earnings pay it down.

name: Hardspace: Shipbreaker
summary: A zero-gravity salvage sim in which the player cuts derelict ships apart with a laser cutter and grapple, manages decompression and volatile systems, and sorts salvage to pay down a large debt.

core_loop: clear land and plant seasonal crops -> water daily and tend livestock -> ship produce for money -> buy animals, seeds, and upgrades -> build relationships and attend festivals -> marry and raise a child before the father's evaluation
design_notes: Director Yasuhiro Wada started the project with three principles (no fighting, uniqueness, and tactile real-time action), and a team of 8 to 10 people at Pack-In-Soft scaled it back to fit SNES limits. The farm rules are forgiving but daily: unwatered crops stop growing instead of dying, chickens need only feed but can die if left outside, and cows must be fed, talked to, brushed, and milked or they sicken. Play is bounded by a two-and-a-half-year term that ends with the father's evaluation of the farm and family, which makes marriage and a child goals alongside crops and livestock.

mechanics.note: Crops need water every day; a missed day halts growth rather than killing the plant, and each crop belongs to a season.
Chickens must be fed and kept indoors or they can die; cows need daily feed, talking, brushing, and milking, and fall sick or die if neglected.
A four-season calendar sets which crops can grow and when festivals occur.
A stamina pool limits work each day; power berries found around the map raise it.
Five eligible women can be courted; marriage and a child count toward the final evaluation.
Villagers' and candidates' affection rises with talking and gifts.
After two and a half years the father evaluates the farm, family, and relationships.
After dark only the bar stays open, so shopping and visits must fit daylight.

name: Harvest Moon
summary: An early farming sim for the Super Famicom in which the player has two and a half years to restore an inherited farm through daily crop watering, livestock care, and courting one of five eligible women.

core_loop: pick national focuses and spend political power -> assign civilian factories to construction and military factories to equipment -> design and train divisions -> draw fronts and battle plans -> divisions fight on supply, terrain, and weather -> capitulate rivals or hold
design_notes: HOI4 separates the industrial war from the field war: civilian factories build capacity and military factories turn resources into equipment, so divisions fight only as well as stockpiles and supply allow. Battle plans let the player act at army-group scale and leave division movement to the AI. National focus trees are the authored branching layer that steers countries toward historical or alternate paths, while battles resolve from unit statistics (proposal stat-combat-resolution).

mechanics.note: Division templates combine battalions (infantry, tanks, cavalry, motorized, mechanized) and support companies, and the mix sets combat statistics and equipment needs; tank, ship, and plane designers added by DLC apply the same idea to equipment.

Supply hubs connect to the capital by railway, with hub capacity set by railway level and limited by the weakest link; supply falls off per province from the hub, and divisions at 35% supply or less suffer attrition and combat penalties.
The player draws front lines and offensive arrows for armies under generals, and the AI moves divisions to carry out the battle plan; divisions can also be ordered directly.

Research runs in parallel slots, and each country has a national focus tree in which one focus at a time is completed for bonuses such as extra factories or events; at launch only Germany, the UK, the USSR, and the US had unique trees.
Military factories turn strategic resources into equipment on production lines, dockyards build ships, and civilian factories build infrastructure and handle trade.
Countries join factions and guarantee others; world tension from 0 to 100 gates what democracies can do.
Mobilization, conscription, and trade laws and ministers are bought with political power.
Ideology popularity among democratic, communist, fascist, and non-aligned groups shifts the government and can end in civil war.
Sea and air regions have weather that affects operations.
Political power accrues over time and is spent on laws such as mobilization, conscription, and trade, on ministers, and on decisions.
States are core or non-core, armies occupy enemy states during war, and peace conferences transfer ownership.
When a country capitulates, winners take turns spending peace conference points on annexation, puppets, and other demands.
Divisions fight in hourly combat rounds comparing attacks against defense or breakthrough, draining organization and strength under terrain, weather, and supply modifiers.

name: Hearts of Iron IV
summary: A World War II grand strategy game starting in 1936 or 1939 in which the player builds factories, turns resources into equipment, designs divisions, follows a national focus tree, and directs fronts and battle plans across land, sea, and air.

core_loop: take email jobs for cash -> buy a rundown house -> clean, demolish, paint, tile, furnish -> buyers evaluate fit and bid -> sell at a profit -> buy bigger properties
design_notes: Each property is judged by a small set of buyer profiles with requirements such as cleanliness or a family room, and their auction bids reward matching a profile rather than maximizing generic quality. Labor is performed with coverage tools (paint roller, mop, window cleaner, plaster tool) that show visible progress, and tool use earns experience spent on faster tools. Email jobs paid by size and quality supply the capital for the first purchase.

mechanics.note: Paint roller, mop, window cleaner, and plaster tool apply coverage to walls, floors, and windows with visible progress; tiling and demolition use the same direct tool loop.
Neighbors send email jobs (cleaning, painting, installing heaters, showers, or air conditioners, furnishing) whose pay depends on job size and quality.
Each property has potential buyers with different needs, such as cleanliness or a family room, who bid according to how well the renovated house suits them.
Sales are resolved by buyers bidding at auction.
Furniture, doors, windows, and wallpaper from a catalog are placed freely.
Using tools earns experience that is spent on tool upgrades that speed up work.

name: House Flipper
summary: A first-person renovation sim in which the player cleans, paints, demolishes, and furnishes rundown houses, then sells them to buyers whose bids depend on how well the house fits their needs.

core_loop: start with water, fire, wind, and earth -> drag two elements together -> look up the pair in the shared database -> if new, a language model names the result and picks an emoji -> result is cached for everyone -> combine the new element further
design_notes: At runtime the model is consulted only on a cache miss: the game checks a global database for the unordered pair, and if no result exists, Llama 2 (later Llama 3.1) generates a short element name, capped at twenty tokens, plus an emoji; the result is stored so the same pair returns the same element to every player. The recipe graph is therefore written collectively and lazily by players and the model, and a First Discovery label marks players who triggered a generation. Pairwise combination discovery is not yet a mechanic in the taxonomy (proposal combination-discovery). It is a boundary case: there is no simulated system beyond the generated recipe graph.

mechanics.note: On a cache miss, a Llama model generates the combined element's name (up to twenty tokens) and emoji; the result is written to a shared database so later requests are deterministic.
Players accumulate discovered elements and First Discoveries, which mark elements no player had made before.
Every action combines two owned elements; on a cache miss a Llama model names the result, the result is stored so every player gets the same answer, and new results earn a First Discovery label.

name: Infinite Craft
summary: A browser crafting game in which combining any two elements yields a new element whose name and emoji a language model generates on first request and a shared database then fixes for all players.

core_loop: create Zois and build homes -> Zois act on needs and personality -> player directs actions or prompts thoughts -> jobs, relationships, rumors, and illness move through the city -> edit the city and generate new items -> share on Canvas
design_notes: inZOI casts the player as an intern at AR Company who manages a city of virtual people and its karma system. It pairs a Sims-style needs model (hunger, hygiene, bathroom, fun, social, energy, sleep, recognition) with city-scale free will that the developers say produces rumors, trends, and disease, plus optional direct control of a Zoi or vehicle. Generative models sit mainly in the creation layer: text prompts generate patterns and images for clothing and furniture, 2D images convert to 3D props, and an on-device small language model lets typed prompts steer a Zoi's thoughts and actions. City-wide progression of unplayed Zois is the offscreen-life-progression mechanic; karma has no mechanic id.

mechanics.note: Eight needs (hunger, hygiene, bathroom, fun, social, energy, sleep, recognition) decay and drive Zois' free-will choices.
Text prompts generate patterns and images for outfits, props, and furniture; 2D images become 3D in-game objects; uploaded video becomes character motion.
An on-device small language model lets the player type prompts that influence a Zoi's thoughts and actions.
Autonomous interactions generate rumors that spread among Zois.
The developers list disease, alongside rumors and trends, among the outcomes that spread through Zois' autonomous interactions.
Personality and life experience shape each Zoi's actions and relationships.
Careers include active jobs played on site.
Zois age and die.
Build mode places walls, roofs, stairs, fences, and gates; city edit changes streets, properties, and weather.
Canvas is the in-game platform for sharing characters, homes, and stories.
Players can switch from point-and-click orders to direct control of a Zoi or a vehicle.

City-wide free will keeps Zois across the city living autonomously while the player directs one household, producing rumors, trends, and disease; the fidelity of the update for distant Zois is not documented.

name: inZOI
summary: A Krafton life sim in early access since March 2025 in which the player oversees autonomous Zois with eight needs in dense cities, with optional on-device language model prompts and generative tools for patterns and objects.

core_loop: join a scheduled official race -> qualify and race on laser-scanned tracks -> incidents and results update Safety Rating and iRating -> license promotion opens higher series -> buy cars and tracks for the next season
design_notes: iRacing grew from Papyrus's NASCAR Racing 2003 Season code with a new tire model and LIDAR-scanned cars and tracks. Its distinctive layer is the competitive structure: a no-fault Safety Rating from incident points per corner gates license classes (Rookie, D, C, B, A, with Pro reserved for esports), an Elo-style iRating sorts drivers into sessions and divisions, and 13-week seasons rotate tracks weekly. Skill rating and matchmaking have no mechanic in the taxonomy (proposed as skill-rating-matchmaking).

mechanics.note: A new tire model replaced the one in the NASCAR Racing 2003 Season code iRacing was built from, and cars and tracks are LIDAR-scanned.
Races are against human drivers on the publisher's servers, so results depend on the driver's braking, throttle, and line precision.
Licenses progress Rookie, D, C, B, A, with Pro for esports qualifiers; promotion depends on a per-discipline Safety Rating computed from incident points and corners per incident.
Cars take damage and tires wear over a race, which pit stops address.

name: iRacing
summary: A subscription online racing sim with laser-scanned cars and tracks in which drivers race scheduled official series and advance through license classes gated by a no-fault Safety Rating, while an Elo-style iRating sorts fields.

core_loop: choose a building from the inventory -> preview its point value from neighbors and terrain -> place it permanently -> score thresholds restock and offer a choice of two packs -> fill the gauge to move to a new island
design_notes: Islanders reduces the city builder to its placement rule: no resources, traffic, citizens, or research, only point values from proximity to compatible structures and natural features and penalties for incompatible ones. Placements are permanent, so each choice consumes space, and the run ends when buildings or space run out before the next threshold. It is included as a boundary case for adjacency scoring, since nothing in the world evolves without the player.

mechanics.note: Each building scores points from nearby compatible buildings and natural features and loses points for incompatible ones; the preview shows the total before placing.
Buildings are placed freely on the island and cannot be removed or built over.
Reaching a point threshold restocks the inventory and offers a choice of two building packs; filling the gauge unlocks a new island.
Each island is procedurally generated.

name: Islanders
summary: A minimalist placement puzzle in which every building scores points from compatible and incompatible neighbors on a procedural island, and score thresholds unlock new building packs and new islands.

core_loop: job bot gives a task -> grab and manipulate objects with tracked hands -> appliances and props react physically -> task completes -> next task until the job ends
design_notes: Included as a boundary case for its interaction model: nearly every object within reach is a physics object that can be picked up, thrown, or combined, and fixed appliances expose buttons, levers, and dials. Tasks are authored and loose, so variety comes from physical improvisation such as choosing pizza toppings or tire styles rather than from a modeled occupation. After all four jobs, modifiers alter the physics.

mechanics.note: Most objects within reach can be picked up and manipulated with tracked controllers, fixed appliances expose buttons, levers, and dials, and post-game modifiers change the physics.
The player's tracked head and hands are the avatar at a room-scale workstation; a smaller human mode adjusts reach.
Four jobs (Office Worker, Gourmet Chef, Store Clerk, Auto Mechanic) each run a sequence of task requests from job bots.

name: Job Simulator
summary: A room-scale VR comedy set in a museum run by robots, where the player performs parodied office, kitchen, store, and garage tasks by grabbing and manipulating physics objects.

core_loop: send expeditions for fossils -> sequence DNA and modify genomes -> incubate dinosaurs -> meet feeding and social needs in enclosures -> guests spend while divisions offer contracts -> contain storms and breakouts -> raise the star rating to unlock islands
design_notes: Jurassic World Evolution turns a park sim into a containment problem. Each species has feeding, social, and territory needs; unmet needs lower comfort, and low-comfort dinosaurs fight, break fences, and escape to attack guests. Three divisions (Science, Security, Entertainment) offer contracts and track reputation, and letting one fall triggers sabotage such as a power shutdown or disease outbreak, which turns faction standing into a source of hazards. Genome modification changes a species' stats, aggression, and appearance, and the player can drive ranger and ACU vehicles to sedate, medicate, transport, and repair. Dinosaurs do not breed in this game; adding modern-species DNA to a genome trades stats against aggression, a rule the taxonomy lacks (proposed as genome-modification).

mechanics.note: Dinosaurs have feeding and social needs plus grassland, forest, and population limits; unmet needs lower comfort, and carnivores hunt herbivores and attack fences and guests.
Science, Security, and Entertainment divisions track reputation; low standing in one triggers sabotage such as power cuts or disease outbreaks.
Each division offers contracts with requirements and rewards that unlock research and story missions.
Storms damage fences and power and set dinosaurs loose; breakouts must be contained before guests are hurt.
Facilities need power from plants through substations; outages open electric fences.
Guests want viewing of varied species plus shopping, food, and amenities, and flee or die during breakouts.
Fossil DNA completion unlocks species, and the research center unlocks buildings, upgrades, and genome modifications.
The Expedition Center sends teams to global dig sites that yield fossils for DNA and for sale.
The player can drive ranger jeeps and ACU helicopters to resupply feeders, repair fences, and tranquilize dinosaurs.
Diseases spread among dinosaurs and must be treated by rangers or ACU.
Island star ratings unlock the next island in the Las Cinco Muertes archipelago.

name: Jurassic World Evolution
summary: A dinosaur park management game in which the player excavates fossils for DNA, breeds and modifies dinosaurs, and keeps them contained through storms, sabotage, and breakouts while balancing three division contracts.

core_loop: wander the world with a squad -> fight, trade, steal, or get captured -> injuries and hunger reduce stats while skills train from use -> recruit and found an outpost -> factions react and world states shift
design_notes: There is no main character: every recruit and NPC is a potential equal, with no hero units given stronger stats, and the world and shops do not scale to the player, so early characters are weaker than most people they meet. Progress comes from use-based skill gain, which makes losing fights a form of training. Deaths of notable faction leaders change world states, such as towns taken over by a new faction. Chris Hunt developed it alone until 2013, and it was one of the first games in Steam Early Access.

mechanics.note: Each limb has its own health; limbs can be damaged or severed and replaced with prosthetic or robotic limbs, and blood loss and injuries reduce stats and movement while squadmates carry the wounded.
Skills rise from the actions they describe, such as stealing for thievery and fighting for combat, with stats and appearance changing as characters grow.
The player commands any squad member directly in real time with pause; no character is privileged, and the squad acts together.
Many factions and species with relations to each other; the player can aid or oppose them, and deaths of notable figures shift world states.
Player standing with each faction changes access and hostility.
Starvation reduces character stats.
Outposts are built and upgraded into fortified havens or businesses.
Squad members keep job lists for base work and production.
