Subgenre is set to city-builder because its lineage is placement and budget puzzles rather than population or evolution modeling. It began as a Ludum Dare 45 entry in October 2019.

mechanics.note: Buildings have placement rules: wind turbines go only on stone tiles and power toxin scrubbers, which clean soil so irrigators can green it.
Each restored tile earns points, and points are the only currency for buildings and upgrades, so a map can stall if spending outruns restoration.
Pumps refill dried riverbeds and tools carve new rivers.
Tools create new rivers and some stone tiles.
Restored biomes attract deer, birds, fish, and bears.
Each map sets restoration targets before the player can recycle buildings and leave.

name: Terra Nil
summary: A reverse city builder in which the player places machines to clean toxic soil, restore water, and grow biomes on a barren map, then recycles every building and leaves.

claims.text: Early access began on 2023-02-10, and version 1.0 released on 2025-10-10 with multiple drones and a revamped tech tree, published by Metaroot.

core_loop: write a drone program -> execute it on the farm grid -> plant, water, and harvest crops -> spend harvests on unlocks -> new language features and crops change what code is worth writing -> optimize for speed and leaderboard times
design_notes: The Farmer Was Replaced teaches programming by making farm labor too slow to do any other way: the drone does nothing unless code tells it to, and the language itself is unlocked piecemeal (loops, variables, functions, lists, dictionaries) with farm expansion and new crops. Execution is metered in simulated ticks rather than real CPU: literals and assignment are free, arithmetic and getters cost 1 tick, and a successful move() costs 200, so optimization means reducing drone actions more than reducing statements. Crops add algorithmic puzzles: polyculture companions requested within three moves multiply yield, harvesting the sunflower with the most petals (out of at least ten) gives eight times the power that doubles drone speed, and mazes and dinosaurs need search-style code. Leaderboards run the player's program as fixed-start simulations totaling at least two hours and score the average time. Code lives in .py files that external editors can edit.

mechanics.note: A Python-like language stored in .py files drives the drone; every operation has a tick cost (arithmetic 1, a successful move 200, a failed action 1) that scales with the speed factor, and Megafarm adds more drones.
Grass, bushes, trees, carrots, pumpkins, cactus, and sunflowers are planted, grown, and harvested by the drone, with Watering and Fertilizer unlocks that act on growth.
Harvested resources buy unlocks with prerequisites, including farm expansion, speed, loops, variables, functions, lists, dictionaries, polyculture, mazes, dinosaurs, and the leaderboard.

Under polyculture, grass, bushes, trees, and carrots request a different companion plant on a tile within three moves, found with get_companion(); planting it multiplies yield, 5x before upgrades and doubling per upgrade.
Leaderboards run the player's program from fixed starts until a resource target is met, repeated to at least two hours, and score the average completion time.
Every operation costs simulated ticks (arithmetic 1, a successful move() 200, a failed action 1), so optimizing means cutting drone actions more than statements.

name: The Farmer Was Replaced
summary: A programming game in which the player writes Python-like code for a farming drone on a grid farm, where every operation costs simulated ticks, and harvests crops to buy unlocks for language features, farm size, more drones, and new crops.

core_loop: read the puzzle goal -> place the supplied parts among fixed objects -> start the machine -> watch the chain reaction -> adjust positions until the goal triggers
design_notes: Each puzzle fixes some objects in a side-view scene and hands the player a small inventory of parts; the solution is a chain reaction where each part triggers the next, such as a ball dropping on a seesaw that frees a mouse that runs toward cheese. The physics engine models gravity and air pressure as global settings and has no random number generator, so a design behaves the same on every run and solutions are verifiable. A freeform mode exposes all parts so players can make puzzles for others.

mechanics.note: Levels supply a limited inventory of parts such as balls, ropes, pulleys, belts, electrical generators, cats, and mice that the player places among fixed objects; parts act on each other by contact, rope, or belt.
A deterministic 2D physics engine with no random number generator moves balls, seesaws, and falling objects under level-set gravity and air pressure, so the same design always gives the same run.
Each puzzle states one simple goal, such as moving an object to a target, that must be met with only the parts provided.
Some parts react to others by fixed rules, such as a mouse running toward cheese.
Electrical generators driven by other parts power electrical devices in the contraption.
Freeform mode saves player-built puzzles, using any part, for others to solve.

name: The Incredible Machine
summary: A Rube Goldberg puzzle game in which the player places supplied parts such as balls, ropes, pulleys, belts, and animals into a level so that a deterministic physics run completes a simple goal.

core_loop: explore a frozen region -> scavenge, hunt, and harvest -> manage calories, thirst, fatigue, and warmth -> weather, night, and wildlife threaten condition -> craft, repair, and shelter -> survive another day until death
design_notes: Survival mode has no zombies or authored goal; the cold, wildlife, and dwindling supplies are the opposition, and death deletes the save. All needs feed a single condition stock: an empty warmth bar drains condition about 20% per hour while empty hunger or fatigue drain about 1% and thirst 2%, so cold is the fast killer and food is the slow one. Time is treated as the scarce resource because every action costs calories and in-game hours. The episodic Wintermute story mode has no permadeath.

mechanics.note: Warmth, fatigue, hunger, and thirst feed one condition stock; when a need is empty, condition drains per hour (warmth 20%, fatigue 1%, hunger 1%, thirst 2%), and afflictions such as hypothermia, frostbite, and dysentery drain or cap it.
Wind, falling temperatures, and blizzards change how fast warmth drops and how far the player can travel; nights are significantly colder.
In Survival mode the save is deleted on death; a later DLC option allows up to three resurrections per save at a difficulty cost, and Misery mode always uses permadeath.
Nights are darker and colder, shaping travel and shelter.
Hides, guts, and wood are crafted into clothing, tools, and arrows.
Clothing and tools lose condition with use and must be repaired.
Food loses condition over time.
Manufactured supplies are finite, so long runs shift from looting to hunting and crafting.

name: The Long Dark
summary: A first-person wilderness survival sim set in frozen northern Canada where the player manages warmth, calories, thirst, fatigue, and afflictions against cold, weather, and wildlife.

core_loop: paint elements onto the grid -> unpause the simulation -> watch particles fall, flow, burn, and react under pressure, heat, and electricity -> adjust or add elements -> save and share the build
design_notes: The Powder Toy combines a per-particle falling-sand layer with coarser fields for air pressure, air velocity, and heat, so explosions push air, air moves powders, and temperature thresholds change element states such as ice to water to steam. Electricity runs through conductive elements via sparks, and players build working logic gates, engines, and nuclear reactors from them. Element count passed 250 by 2025; the source is GPLv3 and the in-game save browser is the main distribution channel for builds.

mechanics.note: Each cell holds one particle of an element such as powder, liquid, gas, or solid, which moves by local rules each frame; element types numbered 258 as of February 2025.
Element pairs react by rule: acid dissolves most materials, acid and base neutralize into salt water, fuels ignite, and neutrons from radioactive elements can drive chain reactions.
Particles carry temperature that conducts to neighbors; melting and boiling thresholds change states, and the heat display shows the field.
A coarser grid of air pressure and velocity moves particles and is pushed by explosions and fans and blocked by walls.
Sparks conduct through metals and semiconductors to power switches, logic gates, and machines built from elements.
Fire and plasma ignite flammable elements and spread through fuel.
An online save browser with votes and comments distributes community builds.
A Lua API adds elements and automation scripts; the source is GPLv3 on GitHub.
The simulation can be paused and stepped frame by frame.

name: The Powder Toy
summary: An open-source falling-sand sandbox where hundreds of elements interact cell by cell under simulated air pressure, heat, gravity, and electricity.

core_loop: build and furnish the lot -> motives decay -> objects advertise motive gains and Sims act or take queued orders -> jobs pay for upgrades -> skills and friendships unlock promotions -> expand house and family
design_notes: Will Wright drew on Christopher Alexander's A Pattern Language, treating a house as a set of functional patterns judged by how well they serve the people living in it. Much of the behavioral logic sits in objects: each object advertises which motives it raises and by how much, and Sims with free will enabled choose among those advertisements weighted by their current motives. Sims are deliberately not fully autonomous, since paying bills, finding jobs, exercising, and having children need explicit commands, so the player alternates between architect and caretaker. Build and Buy modes pause time, separating spatial design from the live simulation.

mechanics.note: Eight motives (Hunger, Comfort, Hygiene, Bladder, Energy, Fun, Social, Room) decay at different rates; low motives drag down mood, and neglect can kill.
Each of the 150-plus base-game objects advertises motive gains (a refrigerator advertises Hunger, a bed Energy), and Sims query the lot's objects to find interactions.
Build and Buy modes freeze time while the player lays walls, floors, and objects on a square tile grid; object quality and layout set how efficiently motives can be met.
Free will scores advertised interactions against current motive levels so the most depleted motive tends to win; players can cancel queued autonomous actions.
Free will is an option toggle; even with it on, bills, job hunting, exercise, and having children need commands.
Twenty-five personality points are split across Neat, Outgoing, Active, Playful, and Nice, which change preferred activities and social outcomes.
Cooking, Mechanical, Charisma, Body, Logic, and Creativity rise through objects such as bookshelves, mirrors, and chess tables, and gate promotions.
Ten career tracks with ten levels each; promotions need skill points and a minimum number of household friends, and change salary and hours.
Every household starts with 20,000 simoleons regardless of size; wages, bills, and purchases set the balance.
Each pair holds a relationship score moved by interactions and eroding without contact; friend counts feed promotions.
Talk, joke, compliment, hug, kiss, tease, slap, and similar interactions succeed or fail on relationship, mood, and personality.
Sims can become partners, marry, and have a baby by explicit command; neglected babies can be taken away by a social worker.
The Room motive reflects lighting, cleanliness, and decorative value around the Sim.
Sims die from neglect or accidents and leave an urn or tombstone; the household continues without them.

name: The Sims
summary: A life sim in which the player builds a house and guides a household of Sims whose decaying motives, personalities, careers, and relationships produce an open-ended domestic story.

core_loop: create a household with aspirations -> wants and fears roll -> direct Sims to meet motives and wants -> aspiration meter and memories shift -> Sims age, marry, and have children who inherit genes -> continue with the next generation
design_notes: The Sims 2 turns the household sandbox into a generational one: babies become toddlers after 3 days, toddlers children after 4, children teens after 8, teens adults after 15, and adults elders after 29, and an elder's remaining life depends on the aspiration meter at the time of aging. Children inherit appearance and personality from both parents through dominant and recessive genes, and each Sim's aspiration (one of eight, such as Romance, Family, Knowledge, or Popularity) biases which wants and fears appear. The wants-and-fears panel is a short-horizon goal generator with no mechanic id yet (proposed as aspiration-wants). SimPE and Body Shop made behavior hacks and custom genetics routine in its mod community.

mechanics.note: Eight motives (Hunger, Comfort, Bladder, Energy, Fun, Social, Hygiene, Environment) decay and push Sims toward objects; failing motives cause refusals and, at the extreme, death.
Objects advertise motive and skill gains that autonomous Sims weigh against their current motive levels.
Seven life stages (baby, toddler, child, teen, young adult with University, adult, elder) advance on fixed day counts; a birthday cake or Grow Up interaction ages a Sim early.
Children inherit eye color, hair color, facial structure, and personality from both parents through dominant and recessive genes; pregnancy lasts 3 Sim days.
Events such as a first kiss, a promotion, or a death are stored as memories that later shape wants and fears.
Twenty-five points are spread over five opposed pairs (Neat/Sloppy, Outgoing/Shy, Active/Lazy, Playful/Serious, Nice/Grouchy); twelve zodiac presets give starting allocations.
Careers have ten levels (25 tracks counting expansions); promotions need skills and a number of family friends, and chance cards can reward or cost the job.
Each pair holds a daily and a lifetime relationship score that move with interactions.
Sims court, marry, and try for babies; Nightlife adds turn-ons and turn-offs shown as up to three chemistry bolts.
Build and Buy modes in a free 3D camera; neighborhood terrain can be imported from SimCity 4.
Elders die of old age and other Sims of accidents or neglect; deaths become memories for survivors.

Each Sim's aspiration (one of eight, such as Romance, Family, Knowledge, or Popularity) biases which wants and fears roll; fulfilled wants fill the aspiration meter, realized fears drain it, and an elder's remaining life depends on the meter.

name: The Sims 2
summary: The 3D sequel to The Sims that adds aging through seven life stages, genetic inheritance, aspirations with wants and fears, and memories, so households play across generations.

core_loop: pick traits and a lifetime wish -> moodlets from events stack into mood -> wishes and opportunities appear -> act across the open town -> earn Lifetime Happiness for rewards -> story progression advances other households
design_notes: Neighborhoods are seamless worlds, so Sims walk between lots without loading screens on PC, and Story Progression keeps households the player is not controlling aging, working, and forming relationships. Personality is a set of up to five discrete traits that unlock and bias interactions, and mood is the sum of moodlets, timed modifiers with named causes. Fulfilled wishes pay Lifetime Happiness points spent on Lifetime Rewards, replacing the wants and fears of The Sims 2. Off-screen story progression and wish generation are captured by the offscreen-life-progression and aspiration-wants mechanics.

mechanics.note: Adult Sims hold up to five traits chosen from a list, replacing the point sliders of earlier games; traits add exclusive interactions and bias autonomous choices.
Moodlets are named, timed mood modifiers (for example Nauseous during pregnancy) whose sum sets mood, which affects performance at work and school.
Six motives (Hunger, Bladder, Energy, Social, Hygiene, Fun) decay and spawn negative moodlets when low.
Objects advertise motive, skill, and fun gains; traits bias which advertisements a Sim picks.
Opportunities arrive from neighbors, community lots, and jobs, such as skill requests or overtime, and pay cash, raises, or relationship gains.
Twelve base careers that branch around level 6, plus part-time jobs; a performance style (Work Hard, Take It Easy, Suck Up to Boss) trades mood against promotion speed.
Ten-level skills such as Logic, Cooking, Painting, Gardening, Writing, Guitar, Athletic, Handiness, Charisma, and Fishing feed careers and opportunities.
Seven life stages with an adjustable lifespan setting.
Conversation menus offer trait- and mood-gated interactions whose acceptance depends on relationship state.
Jobs and school run on fixed hours at rabbit-hole buildings, structuring each household's day.
Build and Buy modes with Create-a-Style, which recolors walls, floors, objects, and clothing with any pattern and material.
Sims die of old age or of fire, starvation, drowning, or electrocution.
A Lifetime Wish is chosen at creation and short-term wishes appear from traits and events; fulfilled wishes pay Lifetime Happiness points spent on Lifetime Rewards.
Story Progression keeps households the player is not controlling aging, working, forming relationships, and moving around the open neighborhood; it can be switched off in the options.

name: The Sims 3
summary: The third mainline Sims game, which places households in a seamless open neighborhood where unplayed Sims keep living, and replaces personality sliders with up to five traits and mood with stacked moodlets.

core_loop: build a home or download one from the Gallery -> moodlets from events and surroundings set the dominant emotion -> emotion unlocks interactions and speeds skills -> pursue aspiration milestones and a career -> earn rewards -> share households and builds
design_notes: The Sims 4 makes emotion the central state: moodlets from actions, events, objects, and social interactions carry an emotion type and weight, and the strongest set the Sim's single dominant emotion, which gates emotional interactions and speeds matching skills. Adult personality is three traits plus a bonus trait from the chosen aspiration, and completing aspiration milestones grants reward traits. Build mode treats rooms as units that can be moved, duplicated, saved to a library, and shared through the Gallery; the base game became free to play on 2022-10-18. Neighborhood Stories, a free update that advances unplayed households, is the offscreen-life-progression mechanic.

mechanics.note: Moodlets carry an emotion type (such as Happy, Focused, Flirty, Angry, Tense, or Sad), an intensity, and a timer; the highest-weighted emotion becomes the Sim's dominant emotion.
Adults hold three traits and children and teens two, plus one bonus trait from the aspiration; traits add moodlets, autonomous behaviors, and exclusive interactions.
Six needs (Hunger, Bladder, Energy, Social, Hygiene, Fun) decay and spawn negative moodlets such as Hungry or Bored when low.

Dominant emotions unlock emotion-specific interactions and raise gain for matching skills (Inspired for creative, Focused for mental, Energized for physical); extreme states such as Hysterical can kill.
Objects advertise need, skill, and emotion gains, and Sims multitask, such as talking while cooking.
Build mode draws walls and rooms, places premade rooms, and moves or duplicates whole rooms.
Sims, households, rooms, and lots can be saved to a personal library and placed again.
The Gallery uploads and downloads Sims, households, rooms, and buildings from other players inside the game.
Newborn, infant, toddler, child, teen, young adult, adult, and elder; toddlers were added in 2017 and newborn and infant in 2023.
Careers require related skills, for example Cooking and Mixology for Culinary.
Separate friendship and romance bars per pair.
Social menus are filtered by emotion and traits, with emotion-specific variants of interactions.
Free will can be toggled; with it off Sims act only on player orders except for urgent needs.
The chosen aspiration grants a bonus trait and a track of milestones whose completion earns reward traits; short-term whims, later reworked as wants and fears, appear from emotions and traits.

Neighborhood Stories, added in a free update, advances unplayed households with events such as moves, relationships, and births, with settings that limit which households and event types it may touch.

name: The Sims 4
summary: The fourth mainline Sims game, built around a dominant emotion computed from moodlets, three-trait personalities with aspiration rewards, multitasking, room-based building, and an in-game Gallery for sharing creations.

core_loop: build rooms from blueprints -> hire and train staff -> patients queue for GP diagnosis and referrals -> treatment cures or kills -> fees and reputation -> research new rooms and meet level goals
design_notes: Theme Hospital turns medicine into routing. The GP and specialist diagnosis rooms raise a patient's diagnosis certainty, and the player sets the threshold at which treatment starts (it can be set above 100%), trading throughput against deaths from wrong cures. Rooms are fixed blueprints that need set furniture and, for some, specialist staff, so the staff roster and the floor plan gate each other. Machines that explode without a handyman, epidemics that can be covered up before the health inspector arrives, and timed emergencies add pressure on top of the queues. Much of the code came from Theme Park; CorsixTH is an open-source reimplementation with a level editor.

mechanics.note: A GP diagnoses or refers patients to specialist diagnosis rooms; treatment starts once certainty passes a player-set threshold, and diseases are fictional, such as Bloaty Head.
Rooms are placed as blueprints with doors and windows, then furnished with required items; many rooms must be researched first.
Doctors, nurses, handymen, and receptionists are hired with performance stats; some rooms need doctors with specialist skills.
Patients queue outside each room; the player can rearrange queues, and long waits push patients to leave.
Doctors can be trained to gain skills and specialisms.
Machines such as the Inflator need handyman servicing or they explode.
Epidemics break out and can be covered up before a health inspector visits; failure brings fines and lost reputation.
Research unlocks rooms, drugs, and machine improvements.
Cures and deaths move a reputation that affects patient intake and level goals.
Staff tire and need breaks under player-set break rules; patients need drinks and toilets.
Emergencies require curing a group of patients within a time limit for a bonus.
Each level sets goals for money, reputation, cures, and hospital value; negative funds or too many deaths lose the level.

name: Theme Hospital
summary: A hospital management game where the player builds rooms, hires and trains staff, and routes patients with comic diseases through diagnosis and treatment to meet level goals.

core_loop: place rides, shops, and paths -> visitors arrive by bus and choose attractions -> tune prices and shop ingredients -> fund research and hire staff -> yearly judging against rivals -> sell the park and buy a plot abroad
design_notes: Theme Park gives every visitor its own record (about 200 bytes each) and lets the player change the product as well as its price: ingredient settings such as sugar in ice cream trade cost against whether customers return. The full-simulation level adds wage and supply negotiations, where failure means staff strikes or lost shipments, plus research funding and shares; the sandbox level removes them, so one engine serves three depths. Unhappy visitors attract thugs, which ties satisfaction to crime. Negotiation has no mechanic in the taxonomy (proposed as negotiation).

mechanics.note: Each visitor is an individual with its own personality and arrives and leaves by bus; unhappy crowds draw thugs who vandalize and attack entertainers.
Entry, ride, and shop prices plus ingredient levels such as sugar in ice cream decide what visitors buy and whether they come back.
Over thirty attractions, shops, toilets, and scenery are placed on a plot, with coasters needing laid-out track.
Rides wear down and explode if mechanics do not maintain them; research can make rides more durable.
Entertainers, security guards, mechanics, and handymen are hired and their wages negotiated; understaffing brings litter, breakdowns, and crime.
Visitors need food, drink, and toilets as their visit goes on.
Visitors queue for rides and shops.
A funding level drives research into new items, ride durability, staff efficiency, and bus capacity.
Thugs appear when visitors are unhappy; security guards counter them.
The park is judged against rival parks each year.
On the full-simulation level, staff wage talks and supply negotiations are haggles; failed wage talks end in strikes and failed supply talks in lost shipments.

name: Theme Park
summary: A theme park management game in which the player builds rides and shops, tunes prices and recipes for individually simulated visitors, and sells parks to expand worldwide.

core_loop: spend the day in the shelter crafting, cooking, trading, and treating -> assign night roles -> one survivor scavenges a location -> encounters force moral choices -> hunger, wounds, illness, and mood shift -> survive until the ceasefire
design_notes: The game turns war into a resource-and-conscience problem: survival needs push the player toward theft or violence, and those acts lower survivors' mood, so material and moral states are coupled. A day-night split separates base management (snipers keep survivors inside by day) from risky scavenging by one chosen survivor, and the length of the war is randomized so the player cannot plan to a known end. The radio reports weather, prices, and war news that let the player anticipate shortages. It draws on the 1992-96 Siege of Sarajevo.

mechanics.note: Snipers confine survivors to the shelter by day for crafting, cooking, and care; at night survivors are assigned to sleep, guard, or scavenge.
Each survivor tracks hunger, fatigue, health, and mood, and the player must keep them up until the ceasefire.

Mood falls with hunger, illness, loss of companions, and morally weighted acts such as stealing or killing; depressed or broken survivors refuse tasks and may leave the shelter or take their own lives.
Scavenging encounters and visitors at the door pose choices, such as robbing vulnerable NPCs or giving away supplies, that trade material gain against mood and each survivor's ending.
Each survivor has one or two traits, such as Good Cook, plus hidden stats.
Workshops craft weapons, alcohol, beds, stoves, and shelter upgrades from scavenged materials.
Radio broadcasts give weather warnings, economic updates, and war news.
Barter values change with conditions announced on the radio.
Winter raises demand for heating fuel.
Neighbors and strangers arrive with requests tied to the shelter's state.
Noisy actions while scavenging at night, such as breaking through obstacles, can alert people at the location.

name: This War of Mine
summary: A survival sim about civilians in a besieged city who maintain a shelter by day, scavenge by night, and face moral choices that change their mood until a randomized ceasefire.

core_loop: dam and channel rivers -> irrigate farms and forests from stored water -> beavers work, eat, and seek wellbeing -> a drought or badtide cuts or poisons the flow -> stockpiles and reservoirs carry the colony through -> build upward and expand
design_notes: Water is a simulated field rather than a resource count: a 2D model adapted from erosion simulation linked each tile to four neighbors by virtual pipes and was replaced by 3D water in Update 6 (October 2024), so dams, floodgates, and canals change where moisture reaches crops. Recurring droughts grow harsher and badtides turn sources into contaminating badwater, so play alternates between building reservoirs and surviving a known dry period. Limited space pushes housing and workshops into vertical stacks, and sensors and relays let players automate floodgates.

mechanics.note: Tiles exchange water through virtual pipes with evaporation; moisture spreads to nearby land and falls off sharply uphill; dams, levees, floodgates, and canals redirect flow.
Recurring droughts switch sources off and badtides release contaminating badwater; both grow harsher over time and are signalled in advance.
Explosives dig tunnels and reshape terrain.
Lodges and workshops stack on platforms; ziplines and tubeways move beavers between levels.
Crops grow only on irrigated soil and fail when it dries.
Beavers need food, water, rest, and wellbeing from diet variety, entertainment, and decorations.
Water tanks and warehouses buffer droughts.
Water wheels and other generators power workshops and bots through a connected network.
Sensors, relays, and counters control dams and factories.

name: Timberborn
summary: A city builder for beaver colonies in which simulated water flows over terrain, recurring droughts and toxic badtides cut or poison it, and players dam, channel, and store water while building upward.

core_loop: draw walls, paths, and building outlines -> procedural rules assemble bricks, roofs, doors, and supports to fit -> reshape terrain and add water -> ivy grows and sheep wander the paths -> keep editing
design_notes: Tiny Glade takes the Townscaper approach to freehand strokes: a path drawn through a building produces a door, and raising a building adds columns and beams to support it, so local rules respond to how elements meet. The two-person studio built it on a custom fork of the Rust engine Bevy. It is a boundary case: the only autonomous elements are ambient life such as growing ivy and wandering sheep.

mechanics.note: Walls, paths, and building outlines are turned into detailed geometry; a path through a building creates a door and raising a building adds supporting columns and beams.
Strokes are drawn freely without a grid.
Terrain height can be changed and rivers and ponds added.

name: Tiny Glade
summary: A medieval building sandbox in which drawn walls, paths, and building outlines are assembled by procedural rules into detailed castles and cottages, with no goals, management, or failure states.

core_loop: add Miis to the apartment -> Miis develop friendships, crushes, and quarrels -> they raise problems such as food, clothes, or advice -> solve problems to fill happiness and earn money -> level-up gifts and new island venues unlock -> couples marry and have children
design_notes: The player is an omnipotent observer who cannot control Miis directly and instead answers their requests, so most of the comedy comes from autonomous pairings and quarrels among Miis whose looks, names, voices, and personalities the player designed. Key relationship changes pass through player consent: the player approves a confession before it happens and resolves fights indirectly. The apartment holds up to 100 Miis, and a filled happiness meter levels a Mii up and earns it a present, so care is paced by a stream of small templated problems rather than decaying meters.

mechanics.note: Miis form friendships and conflicts on their own; pairs can grow closer, fall into fights, or break up, and the player intervenes only indirectly.
Opposite-gender friends of similar age may develop crushes; the player approves the confession, couples can marry and have a child who later moves in or leaves via StreetPass.
Miis raise problems such as wanting a food or outfit, needing relationship advice, or asking for a minigame; solving them raises happiness and pays money.
Each Mii receives a personality at creation that shapes its behavior.
Adding Miis and completing objectives unlocks shops, an amusement park, a concert hall, a café, and other venues.
Miis can be imported from Mii Maker or by scanning QR codes.
StreetPass sends grown children to other players' islands.
Island time follows the 3DS clock; at night the player can listen to sleeping Miis' dreams.

name: Tomodachi Life
summary: A Nintendo 3DS life sim in which player-made Mii characters live in an island apartment building, form friendships, quarrels, and romances on their own, and ask the player to solve their problems.

core_loop: click to add or remove a colored block on the irregular grid -> the solver picks modules for that cell and its neighbors -> arches, stairs, roofs, and gardens appear -> keep editing
design_notes: The grid is a subdivided, jittered hex grid of irregular quads, and each edit triggers a real-time wave function collapse that narrows the valid corner modules for the changed cells and their neighbors before decoration is applied. The player expresses only occupancy and color; all architectural detail is derived, which makes the game a pure case of procedural build assist. It is a boundary case because nothing evolves without the player; its author calls it more of a toy than a game.

mechanics.note: Each block edit reruns a marching-cubes-style module lookup and a wave function collapse over affected cells, then adds windows, chimneys, and bushes; delay grows with structure size.
Colored blocks are added or removed anywhere on the grid, stacked vertically.
Enclosed areas are detected and filled with gardens rather than paving.

name: Townscaper
summary: A town-building toy in which clicking colored blocks onto an irregular grid lets a wave function collapse solver assemble houses, arches, stairways, bridges, and gardens, with no goals or resources.

core_loop: survey towns and industries -> build stations, track, roads, docks, and airports -> give vehicles order lists -> payment by cargo, distance, and delivery time -> station ratings and towns grow -> replace aging vehicles and expand
design_notes: Transport Tycoon extends Railroad Tycoon to four transport modes on one isometric map and makes cargo value decay with transit time, so mail suits short or fast routes while coal keeps its value over long hauls. Stations only collect from nearby towns and industries, and a station rating decides how much of an industry's output it receives, which rewards frequent, fast service. Vehicles lose reliability with age and new models arrive on a timeline from 1930 to 2030 (1950 to 2050 in Deluxe), so the fleet must be renewed; date-driven model availability is proposed as dated-tech-timeline. Town councils rate each company through the Local Authority system, which can block new stations. OpenTTD, a reverse-engineered reimplementation first released in 2004, continues the design.

mechanics.note: Trains, road vehicles, ships, aircraft, and helicopters run order lists between stations; revenue depends on cargo type, distance, quantity, and delivery time.
Stations accept and supply cargo only within a catchment around them, and station ratings set how much nearby industries hand over.
Vehicle reliability falls with age, breakdowns become more frequent, and vehicles must be serviced and eventually replaced; prototypes offer better specs with reliability risk.
Primary industries feed secondary ones and finished goods go to towns; poorly served industries can close.
Bi-directional signals in the original; Deluxe adds one-way signals.
Some resource sites run out and new ones appear.
Local Authority ratings per town fall with poor service and tree clearing and can block demolition and new stations.
Towns offer subsidies for serving specific routes.
Up to seven AI transport companies compete for the same towns and industries.
Deluxe adds trading company shares and buying out competitors.
The company starts with an interest-bearing loan.
Road vehicles use town roads and player-built roads from depots.
Revenue per delivery depends on cargo type, quantity, distance, and transit time; mail and passengers lose value quickly while coal tolerates long, slow hauls.
Road, rail, sea, and air models are introduced on a timeline from 1930 to 2030 (1950 to 2050 in Deluxe), new models carry reliability risk, and aging fleets must be renewed as better models arrive.
Rail track, including slopes, bridges, and tunnels, is laid piece by piece on the isometric tile map, with costs for terrain changes and demolition.

name: Transport Tycoon
summary: A transport business sim in which the player builds road, rail, sea, and air networks between towns and industries over a century, earning by delivery speed and distance while vehicles age and break down.

core_loop: build housing, jobs, and services across the islands -> each citizen's happiness and faction alignment shift with conditions -> issue edicts, trade, and raid to fund the treasury -> advance through four eras -> win elections or suppress rebels to stay in power
design_notes: Tropico couples a conventional production and services city builder to a political layer: each simulated citizen holds happiness and faction alignments, and those aggregate into election results and rebel recruitment. Edicts and policies trade one faction's approval against another's, so building decisions double as political ones. Tropico 6 moves play to an archipelago joined by bridges from the World Wars era onward and organizes progress into Colonial, World Wars, Cold War, and Modern eras.

mechanics.note: Political factions each approve or disapprove of El Presidente based on conditions and decisions that match their ideology.
Elections can be held or rigged; losing one removes El Presidente and ends the game.
Each citizen's happiness across categories such as food, housing, and liberty aggregates into approval.
Edicts with costs and effects on factions and citizens.
Low approval breeds rebels, protests, and coup attempts.
Buildings placed freely across the islands; bridges connect islands from the World Wars era.
Exports through docks fund the treasury.
Skilled jobs require citizens with high school or college education.
Relations with foreign powers affect trade and aid.

name: Tropico 6
summary: A political city builder in which El Presidente develops an island archipelago across four eras while individually simulated citizens' happiness and faction loyalties decide elections, protests, and revolts.

core_loop: build and decorate rooms -> hire staff with traits and train qualifications -> patients flow from GP to diagnosis to treatment -> cures earn money and reputation -> research and Kudosh unlock items -> earn stars to open the next hospital
design_notes: Two Point Hospital keeps Theme Hospital's room-blueprint and diagnosis-pipeline structure and adds a deeper staff layer: every hire has personality traits, a specialisation, and trainable qualifications, so the training room is a second production line beside the clinical one. Room prestige rises with room size and decoration and feeds staff happiness, which links interior design to staff retention. Progress spreads across many hospitals with one-to-three-star goals, and items unlock with Kudosh, a currency earned from challenges rather than money. Assistants can run marketing campaigns (proposed mechanic advertising-awareness).

mechanics.note: Patients start in a GP's Office and move through further diagnostic rooms until diagnosed, then to a treatment room; illnesses are comic, such as Light-Headedness and Mock Star.
Doctors, nurses, janitors, and assistants come with personality traits and specialisations that change performance; wages and morale must be managed.
Patients queue at rooms while their health falls; untreated patients die, and long waits lower satisfaction.
Rooms are drawn and furnished with required machines, plus corridors with toilets, cafes, vending machines, and staff rooms.
Staff earn qualifications in the training room that unlock or improve tasks.
Staff traits change efficiency and behavior.
Room prestige depends on size and decoration and affects staff happiness.
Patients and staff need toilets, food, drinks, and rest.
Later levels bring epidemics with a limited vaccine supply; immunizing every infected patient earns a reward.
Machines degrade and need janitor maintenance.
The Research room unlocks new rooms and machine upgrades.
Kudosh from challenges unlocks items; one star unlocks the next hospital.
Each hospital has star objectives; extra objectives raise the rating to two or three stars.
Steam Workshop support added in 2019.
Assistants in the marketing room run paid campaigns that draw more patients, optionally targeted at specific illnesses.

name: Two Point Hospital
summary: A hospital management game and spiritual successor to Theme Hospital in which the player builds rooms, trains staff with traits and qualifications, and cures comic illnesses across a chain of hospitals.

core_loop: practice skills by using them -> gather resources and craft goods -> trade with other players -> build and furnish a house -> fight monsters or other players -> recover from death and re-equip
design_notes: Ultima Online tried to simulate a world rather than a set of classes: skills grow with practice, goods come from player crafting, and houses persist on the map. Its planned artificial-life ecology, in which animal behavior responded to ecological events, was removed during beta because players killed creatures faster than they could spawn. Unrestricted player killing at launch led to the 2000 Trammel and Felucca split into consensual and open PvP facets, an early rule-zoned world (proposal pvp-security-zones); fans later reverse-engineered it to build server emulators.

mechanics.note: Progression is skill-based with no levels or classes; skills improve as the character uses them, so a character's abilities record what the player has practiced.
Shards keep persistent player houses and goods; unrestricted PvP at launch was split in 2000 into a consensual-PvP Trammel facet and an open-PvP Felucca facet.
The economy is craft-based: players gather materials and craft the weapons, armor, and goods other players buy.
Player guilds such as Shadowclan formed persistent communities.
Criminal acts against other players carry consequences whose rules changed over the game's life.
Players place houses on open land in the shared world.
A dead character leaves a corpse that other players can loot; item insurance, added in 2003, keeps chosen items for a fee.
The 2000 Renaissance expansion split the world into Trammel, where player-versus-player combat is consensual, and Felucca, where it is open.

name: Ultima Online
summary: A persistent fantasy MMO in which players progress through skills without classes or levels, craft goods for a player-driven economy, own persistent houses, and could attack each other anywhere until the 2000 split into Trammel and Felucca.

core_loop: load or build a system -> set masses, positions, and time step -> run gravity forward -> watch orbits, collisions, and climate respond -> tweak parameters or add bodies
design_notes: Every body attracts every other under Newtonian n-body gravity, so the player can test questions such as what happens if a star passes the Solar System and see the answer rather than read it. The current version (a rewrite released as Universe Sandbox 2 in 2014 and renamed in 2018, still in early access) adds composition from a small set of materials, collisions that leave molten craters, and a climate layer where sea ice tracks axial tilt and oceans boil near a star. The simulation is an instrument for parameter sweeps; there are no goals or agents.

mechanics.note: Newtonian n-body gravity acts between all bodies; the player edits mass, density, radius, and velocity and watches orbits, ejections, spin-apart breakup, and collisions follow.
Simulation speed runs from real time to years per second and can be paused; larger time steps trade against accuracy, so fast runs can diverge from slow ones.
Surface temperature, sea ice, and oceans respond to stellar distance and axial tilt; moving a planet can freeze or boil it.
Collisions and stellar irradiance heat bodies, shown as molten surfaces and temperature maps.
Planets are composed from materials such as water, rock, iron, and gases, and oceans and mountains can be shaped.
Orbit trails and surface temperature maps expose state that is otherwise invisible.
Player-made simulations are shared on Steam Workshop.

name: Universe Sandbox
summary: A space physics sandbox where the player builds and alters star systems and watches Newtonian n-body gravity, collisions, and simplified planetary climate play out at adjustable speed.

claims.disputes: Release year: 1982 per Wikipedia versus 1981 per Guinness World Records and the original skeleton. This entry uses 1982, the dated release.
claims.text: Wikipedia's infobox and lead date the Intellivision release to 1982-06-03 (Aquarius port 1983), while Guinness World Records names Utopia, released on the Intellivision in 1981, as the first city-building videogame.

core_loop: spend gold on houses, farms, factories, forts, and boats -> round timer runs while boats fish and clouds rain on farms -> end-of-round income and score from population welfare -> rebels, storms, and pirates strike -> next round
design_notes: Utopia runs as up to 50 real-time rounds of 30 to 120 seconds, so the turn boundary is a clock rather than a player action; income from factories arrives at round end while fishing and rain income depend on what happens during the round. Two players share one screen with no AI opponent, and each can fund rebels on the other's island or sink the other's fishing boat with a PT boat, so the welfare score is contested directly. It is commonly cited as the first city-building game, though its release year is disputed between 1981 and 1982.

mechanics.note: Each player places houses, schools, factories, hospitals, and forts on tiles of their own island, paid for with gold bars.
Rounds last 30 to 120 seconds for up to 50 rounds; factory output pays out and the score updates at each round's end.
Points depend on population and how well it is housed, fed, and kept happy; neglect lowers the score and invites rebellion.
Rebels reduce the score and can destroy buildings; a rival can pay gold to fund rebels on the other island.
Randomly generated rain clouds earn income when they pass over a player's farms; tropical storms and hurricanes also occur.
Fishing boats earn income only while positioned over a moving school of fish.
Players steer fishing boats and PT boats directly; PT boats sink the opponent's fishing boat.
Gold bars are the single currency for all construction.

name: Utopia
summary: A two-player Intellivision strategy game in which rival island rulers spend gold on buildings and boats in timed rounds, scoring points for how well their populations are housed, fed, and kept content.

core_loop: explore seeded biomes -> gather wood, stone, and ore -> build shelters that must be supported and roofed -> eat food for health and stamina -> craft better gear -> summon and defeat each biome's boss -> sail to harder biomes
design_notes: Food is a reward rather than a punishment: eating raises maximum health and stamina and speeds regeneration, and there is no starvation, so the survival layer pushes players toward better food rather than threatening death. This consumable-buff model does not fit survival-meters cleanly (proposal filed). Building uses a support model in which stability falls with distance from the ground, so architecture follows material limits, and uncovered wood decays to half durability in rain. Progression is gated by eight bosses, each summoned with an offering. Early access began in February 2021 and 1.0 shipped in September 2026.

mechanics.note: Stability runs from blue (grounded) to red; it falls with horizontal and vertical distance from ground, a piece cannot exceed its support's stability, and vertical limits are 16 m for wood and stone and 24 m for core wood.
Each world is generated from a seed and divided into biomes (Meadows, Black Forest, Swamp, Mountains, Plains, Ocean, Mistlands, Deep North, Ashlands), each with its own resources, enemies, and boss.
Workbenches, forges, and other stations craft tools, weapons, and building pieces; new materials unlock new recipes.
Food raises maximum health and stamina for a time instead of causing starvation; stamina drains when running or attacking.
Skills rise to level 100 through use and affect damage and stamina drain; dying reduces skill levels.
Comfort from nearby furnishings lengthens the Rested buff.
Each boss leaves a trophy that grants a power at a central altar and opens the next tier of materials.
Uncovered or submerged wood decays to 50% durability; tools lose durability.
Rain wets the player and rots exposed wood.
Random events send enemies against bases.
Some animals can be tamed and bred.
On death the player's equipment and inventory stay in a tombstone at the death site, and skill levels drop, so the player must travel back to recover gear.

name: Valheim
summary: A co-op Viking survival game in a seeded procedural world of biomes where players gather, build structurally supported shelters, eat for stat buffs, and defeat biome bosses to progress.

core_loop: choose a character and episode -> practices offer actions for the situation -> player acts or waits -> other agents simulate each option and take the best for their desires -> emotions, evaluations, and relationships update -> the episode reaches an outcome
design_notes: Richard Evans and Emily Short built Versu around social practices: recurring situations such as a meal or a conversation written as reactive joint plans that offer actions to participants without controlling them. Each agent tests a candidate action by applying it to the world state, scoring the result against its desires (over 300 in total), and undoing it, which the authors contrast with the estimated consequences used in The Sims. World state is a set of exclusion-logic sentences, and the Praxis language with a stress tester that runs hundreds of simulated instances supported over 1,000 parameterized actions. Linden Lab cancelled the project in early 2014; social practices have no mechanic id and are proposed as social-practices.

mechanics.note: Agents score each available action by executing it on the world state, evaluating the result against their desires, and undoing it; the best-scoring action is taken.
Social practices such as a dinner party or a conversation offer role-specific actions with preconditions, and most actions change how characters regard each other.
Agents hold evaluations of each other on roles such as attractiveness or breeding, which actions raise or lower.
Fine-grained emotions on Ekman's typology record their target and cause.
Character files assign each agent desires that weight its action scoring.
A drama manager agent can act to push an episode's authored plot.

name: Versu
summary: A 2013 iPad interactive story platform from Linden Lab in which the player controls one character among autonomous agents who choose actions by simulating their outcomes against hundreds of desires within authored social practices.

core_loop: queue construction of buildings -> buildings hire pops and run production methods -> goods trade at shifting market prices -> wages and needs set standard of living and interest-group support -> enact laws and pursue diplomatic plays -> expand industry
design_notes: Victoria 3 moves the player's main lever from units to the economy: the player queues construction and sets laws, and pops, prices, and wages respond, while armies are handled by generals assigned to fronts. Politics is an output of economics, since pops' economic status sets their interest-group affiliation and political strength. Diplomatic plays turn war declaration into a timed escalation of demands and counter-demands with a chance to back down (proposal crisis-escalation).

mechanics.note: Pops' political strength, from wealth and enfranchisement, flows into interest groups such as the Devout, Industrialists, and Rural Folk; clout is each group's share of the national total, approval comes from laws and government membership, and enacting a law runs phases whose advance or stall chances depend on group endorsement.
Buildings such as mines, farms, and factories convert input goods to outputs; switchable production methods change the input mix, output, and which professions are employed.

Each good has a base price, and the market price moves with the ratio of buy orders from consumption to sell orders from production, scaled by market access from infrastructure; prices feed back into building profitability, wages, and pops' cost of living.
The population is stored as pops by profession, culture, and religion in lower, middle, and upper strata, each with its own wages, needs, and political leanings.
Pops buy goods to meet needs, and the share met sets their standard of living.
Buildings hire pops by profession and qualification, so labor shortages throttle new industry.
Laws such as Free Trade and Laissez-Faire change economic and political rules.
Pops whose needs fall short become radicals, and radical interest groups can start a revolutionary movement with a revolution clock.
Diplomatic plays present a demand, allow counter-demands, run a countdown to mobilize and gather backers, and become war if unresolved.
Technologies such as the Atmospheric Engine unlock buildings and production methods.
Nested tooltips break values into contributing modifiers, extended to battle and market calculations.
Authority, influence, and bureaucracy are capacities with monthly supply and ongoing usage: decrees draw on authority and diplomatic pacts on influence.

Pops carry a culture and a religion; over time pops assimilate toward primary cultures and convert toward the state religion, and citizenship and church laws decide which identities face discrimination.
States change hands through diplomatic plays and wars, and newly acquired states are incorporated over time before they count fully.
Each side's war support falls with exhaustion until one capitulates or the sides settle on the demands from the diplomatic play.

name: Victoria 3
summary: An economic grand strategy game set from 1836 to 1936 in which the player industrializes a nation by building production chains, passing laws through interest-group politics, and pursuing diplomatic plays while population strata respond through wages, needs, and radicalism.

core_loop: dig, plant, and water the garden -> species outlines appear when appear requirements are met -> resident requirements turn visitors into residents -> residents meet romance requirements and lay eggs -> predators and sours disrupt -> sell or trade piñatas -> attract new species
design_notes: Viva Piñata turns habitat suitability into a readable checklist: each species has staged appear, visit, resident, and romance requirements, shown as a black-and-white outline that fills in when residency is met. Because piñatavores must eat other piñatas to become residents or breed, attracting one species can consume another, so the garden is a hand-built food web the player tunes by fencing, spacing, and timing. Sours and Professor Pester's ruffians supply authored pressure, and romance requirements can be bypassed with candy once a species has bred, trading early difficulty for collection speed.

mechanics.note: Each of the 60 species has staged requirements (garden contents, plants, water, terrain, or having eaten a specific item) that turn an outline into a visitor and then a resident.
Piñatavores must eat other piñatas to become residents or breed, and visiting predators eat residents to meet their own requirements.

Two residents of a species that meet romance requirements perform a romance dance and a maze minigame that yields an egg; piñatas are ungendered, and candy skips romance requirements after a species' first romance.
The journal of 60 species, each with requirements to discover, is the long-term goal structure.
Seeds sown with tools grow into flowers, vegetables, and trees that species eat or require; weeds spread and destroy vegetable rows if not removed.
The shovel and other tools plough soil, dig ponds, and sculpt terrain.
Eggs and piñatas could be sent to other players over Xbox Live.

name: Viva Piñata
summary: A garden sim in which the player shapes terrain, plants, and water to attract 60 piñata species, then meets each species' requirements to make them residents, breed them, and manage the predators among them.

claims.text: The Steam page discloses AI-driven NPC text and voice chat that responds to player input in real time; global PC release was 2025-11-14.

core_loop: explore the open world -> talk to NPCs in free text or voice -> take quests and fights -> build reputation and skills -> explore further
design_notes: Included as a boundary case for natural-language interaction at scale. The Steam AI disclosure describes NPC text and voice chat generated in real time from player input. The main questline and combat remain authored and rule-based, so the language model sits beside the simulation rather than inside its state.

mechanics.note: Players type or speak to NPCs and receive live generated replies, per the game's Steam AI disclosure.
Third-person martial-arts traversal and combat.

name: Where Winds Meet
summary: An open-world martial-arts RPG whose NPCs answer free-text and voice chat through a live language model, included as an early large-audience deployment of runtime LLM characters.

claims.text: Anuttacon, the developer, was formed in late 2023 by Cai Haoyu, and Whispers from the Star is its first game.

core_loop: Stella calls, texts, or sends voice messages about her situation -> player answers by voice or text -> model generates her spoken reply and choice -> her choices change whether she survives the situation -> story advances
design_notes: At runtime a model generates Stella's side of every exchange: the player's microphone or text input is answered with dialogue and a fully voiced performance that Anuttacon says was created in collaboration with an actor, with safety filters screening output. The store page says there is no script and that the player's words shape her choices and her survival, so advice acts as an indirect control on an agent the player cannot command. The surrounding structure is linear and story-driven per its store tags, which makes it a hybrid of authored situations and generated conversation. Anuttacon was formed in late 2023 by miHoYo co-founder Cai Haoyu, and this is its first game. It is a boundary case: the only simulated state is the conversation and Stella's choices.

mechanics.note: Open-ended conversation by voice (a microphone is required for the full experience) or text over Stella's communicator, through video calls, voice messages, and texts.
An AI model generates Stella's dialogue and voiced performance in real time, constrained by safety filters, and her in-story decisions follow from what the player says.
The store tags the game as linear and story-rich, so generated conversation plays out inside a sequence of survival situations.

name: Whispers from the Star
summary: A voice-driven sci-fi narrative game in which the player helps stranded astronaut Stella survive on the planet Gaia through open-ended spoken or typed conversation answered by an AI-generated, voiced performance.

core_loop: set up construction offices and deliver materials to sites -> extract and process over 30 commodities by truck, rail, conveyor, and pipe -> house citizens near jobs and transit -> supply food, clothing, heat, and services to keep health, happiness, and loyalty -> export at customs for rubles or dollars -> import what the republic lacks
design_notes: Workers & Resources treats construction itself as logistics: buildings and roads need delivered concrete, steel, and prefab panels plus workers from the player's construction offices, or imported foreign labor at a cost, a system the taxonomy lacks (see run proposal). Over 30 commodities move by mode suited to their form (pipes and tanks for liquids, conveyors and trucks for ores, covered vehicles for goods), so freight network design is the main puzzle. Trade runs through East and West customs houses, flooding one bloc's market lowers returns, and heating demand rising in winter ties utilities to the calendar.

mechanics.note: Over 30 commodities are extracted, processed, and stored in staffed plants.
Trucks, trains, ships, and aircraft are assigned to depots and routes that move goods and workers between buildings.
Exports and imports pass through customs houses at Eastern (rubles) and Western (dollars) borders.
Conveyors move ores and bulk goods between facilities.
Liquids, water, and heating travel through pipes and tanks.
Buses, trams, trains, subways, ships, and planes carry citizens.
Rail signals and interchanges govern shared track.
Flooding one market lowers returns there.
Citizens need food, clothing, and alcohol from shops.
Health and happiness decide whether citizens stay; low loyalty raises crime and lowers work efficiency.
Optional complex education gates skilled jobs.
Optional seasons raise heating demand in winter.

name: Workers & Resources: Soviet Republic
summary: A planned-economy city builder in which every building, commodity, and citizen moves through explicit logistics, from construction materials delivered by truck to exports at border customs for rubles or dollars.

core_loop: pick or design an aircraft -> set location and weather -> fly by hand or autopilot -> blade-element forces respond to geometry and air -> land -> revise the aircraft in Plane Maker
design_notes: X-Plane uses blade element theory: wings, control surfaces, and propellers are split into elements and aerodynamic forces are computed on each from geometry, rather than looked up from performance tables, so an aircraft drawn in the bundled Plane Maker flies according to its shape. That approach underpins its use in FAA-approved training systems when paired with suitable hardware. A plugin SDK exposes simulator data for instruments, cockpits, and external hardware.

mechanics.note: Blade element theory splits wings, control surfaces, and propellers into small elements and computes aerodynamic forces on each from geometry and physical parameters.
Plane Maker lets users define aircraft geometry and components and then fly the result in the simulator.
X-Plane 12 reworked clouds, turbulence, and atmospheric effects, and version 12.3 added a weather-radar system.
The plugin SDK lets developers read simulator data and add instruments, cockpit interfaces, and hardware support.

name: X-Plane
summary: A flight sim whose flight model computes forces on small elements of each wing, control surface, and propeller from aircraft geometry, used for entertainment and in FAA-approved training devices.

core_loop: spot a landmark -> climb, glide, or ride toward it under stamina limits -> solve shrines and fights with physics and elemental interactions -> gather and cook ingredients -> replace broken weapons -> push farther into the world
design_notes: The game is mostly authored content (map, shrines, story) and is included for its systemic layer. A modified Havok physics engine and a separate chemistry engine give objects material properties, so fire burns grass and creates updrafts, metal draws lightning and conducts electricity, wind carries flames and gliders, and cold or heat drains health unless countered by clothing or cooked food. Weapon durability and stamina force continual scavenging and route choice, and shrine puzzles accept any solution that satisfies the physical end condition.

mechanics.note: The chemistry engine gives objects properties such as flammable, metallic, or conductive; fire ignites wood and grass, metal attracts lightning in storms and conducts electricity, and ice melts near fire.

A modified Havok engine moves crates, boulders, and weapons; Magnesis lifts metal objects, Stasis freezes an object so stored hits launch it, and Cryonis raises ice pillars from water, giving shrines and fights unscripted solutions.
A stamina wheel limits sprinting, climbing, swimming, and gliding; hearts are health, and ambient cold and heat damage the player without matching clothing or elixirs.
Fire spreads across grass in the wind direction and produces updrafts that the paraglider can ride.
Rain makes surfaces too slippery to climb, and thunderstorms strike metal equipment with lightning.
Region temperature and fire sources set a temperature gauge that damages the player beyond tolerance.
Cooking combines up to five ingredients in a pot into meals or elixirs whose effects and duration depend on the ingredients.
Weapons, bows, and shields lose durability with use and shatter; the Master Sword recharges instead.
Time of day changes enemy and creature activity, and the Blood Moon respawns defeated enemies.
Link can climb almost any surface, glide, ride horses, and use runes.

name: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild
summary: An open-world action adventure whose physics and chemistry engines let fire, wind, electricity, temperature, and material properties combine, so puzzles and fights accept solutions the designers did not script.

core_loop: fence an exhibit -> match terrain, foliage, rocks, shelter, and toys to the species -> animals grow happy and breed -> guests visit, spend, and react -> awards and income -> research and adopt more animals
design_notes: Zoo Tycoon's core rule is exhibit suitability: each species reports how well its exhibit's terrain mix, foliage, rocks, shelters, toys, and keeper care match its needs, and that suitability drives animal happiness. Guest happiness depends on animal happiness, the species on show, buildings, and scenery, so the two satisfaction meters are chained. Failures are physical: incompatible species in one exhibit kill each other, fences decay, and escaped animals attack guests and staff. Too many complaints about unhappy animals block new adoptions until habitats are fixed.

mechanics.note: Each species has preferred terrain types, foliage, rocks, shelters, toys, and companions; suitability drives happiness, and incompatible species in one exhibit kill each other.
Guest happiness depends on the animals on show, their happiness, buildings such as restrooms and shops, and scenery.
Animals need food, water, cleaning, and keeper attention that keepers supply on rounds.
Fences, paths, buildings, foliage, and scenery are placed on a tile map.
Fences decay and must be repaired by maintenance workers to prevent escapes.
Zookeepers, maintenance workers, and tour guides are hired.
In freeform mode, money spent on research unlocks animals, buildings, and scenery.
Scenarios set targets such as a guest happiness level, exhibit suitability, animal count, or breeding a species.
Animals breed when content; babies grow into adults.
Scenery such as topiary, lamp posts, and benches gives a small guest happiness boost.

name: Zoo Tycoon
summary: A zoo management game in which the player builds exhibits whose terrain, foliage, shelters, and toys must suit each species, balancing animal happiness against guest happiness and income.
